title: Web map with selectable tasks in mobile map view
body:
Working Web map in mobile view on Android device, from which users can:
- See available tasks
- Click on tasks, triggering a mechanism allowing them to select the task and launch ODK Collect with the appropriate project, app user, and form configured.

title: Launch ODK Collect from mobile map view rather than by QR code
body:
# Launch ODK Collect with appropriate configuration from Intent

Ideally we want to launch a specific ODK form from the FMTM. Basically we want the field mapper to select an area/task on a Web map, and quickly end up within ODK with the relevant App User/form/map file cued up.

# What works now
At the moment, a workflow that does the job is:
- The field mapper selects an area on a Web map. A popup appears with a QR code.
- If the web map is displayed on a separate device (a computer, or someone else's phone), the field mapper opens ODK Collect, scans it, and proceeds. However, generally speaking we don't expect field mappers to be carrying a laptop, or to have a colleague with another phone/device next to them. They are mostly likely looking at the Web map on the same phone/device that they are using to fill out the form using ODK Collect.
- From their own phone, they can:
  - Long-press on the QR code and select Download image
  - Open ODK Collect, hit the colored-circle-with-a-letter-in-it project button on the upper right, select Add project
  - Click the kebab menu on the upper right, select Import QR code (seems to be the only option in that menu)
- On the devices we've tested, the resulting dialogue defaults to displaying "Recent images," with the freshly-downloaded QR code as the first (upper left) option. Upon selecting it, ODK Collect switches immediately to the desired project and form.

Thats ok, but it's not awesome. There are two main drawbacks:
- From the "Add project" dialogue, it's not obvious that the kebab menu allows importation of a QR code that's locally saved as an image, and
- The whole process seems like a fair number of button presses.
# What we'd like
It would be delightful if the field mapper could simply click on a Web map, see an ODK icon with a human-readable project ID, click it, get an Android notification along the lines of "Open this link with..." (with ODK Collect as an option, ideally the default or configurable as such) and rock on.

The [Discussion in this thread on the ODK Forum](https://forum.getodk.org/t/launching-collect-from-a-browser/39052) suggests launching from form already found in the instances directory—this seems like something we could build upon. However, it seems like it has a few drawbacks:

- The form must already be present in the instances directory on the field mapper's phone
- I'm not sure if this handles other options, such as basemap (we want an OSM/Mapbox basemap rather than Google) that the QR code handles so admirably.

title: Marking a previously selected task as complete
body:
# Marking a previously selected task as complete

Once a mapper has selected a task, they'll probably be working primarily from ODK Collect to select individual features and collect data on them. When they complete the data collection on all features in the task area, they need to mark the area as complete, ready for validation.

It may be worth considering prompting for this when the ODK Central server sees a number of submissions corresponding to the number of features (or perhaps even when there are verifiably submissions for all of the features in the GeoJSON file representing the features), but this is not necessary for Minimum Viable Product (MVP). 

All that we really need is for the mapper to be able to:
- See the Web map with their currently-selected task obviously visible, and
- Mark it done, which results in:
  - The Campaign Manager and/or Validation team are informed that they have work to do, and
  - The square is marked "Ready for validation" in the Web map for all to see, the mapper can choose another task.

title: Un-select a task (without completing it)
body:
# Un-select a task without completing it

Sometimes a field mapper will select a task by mistake, or for some reason not wish or be able to complete it. In this case, they need a way to unmark it as selected, but ideally without indicating that it's complete and ready for validation.

title: Splitting an AOI into individual tasks
body:
# Splitting an Area of Interest (AOI) into individual tasks

Choosing how to divide an area into tasks for field mapping is an interesting challenge. The [HOT Tasking Manager](http://tasks.hotosm.org/) for remote mapping divides an area of interest into a grid of squares. Remote mappers can use their computer screen to float virtually in the air above their task area, but field mappers must physically visit every point in their task area! Crossing rivers, railways, and trunk roads is inconvenient and sometimes dangerous. Therefore a grid of squares—which ignores physical access issues—is not great for field mapping.

We would like to evaluate different automated strategies to divide an Area of Interest into individual tasks for field mapping. This problem really has two distinct parts:
- What are the most convenient shapes for subdivisions for given types of field mapping tasks?
- How can we automate subdivision into those shapes, in a way that works and produces a reasonable result for many different settings?

[This document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wWu8WkRmFokO5naskexvTfUOiTfULv6Rz3-3O2g6KA0/edit?usp=sharing), which describes a crowdsourcing campaign to implement a good algorithm (an idea that we're proposing to help involve a wide range of community developers and volunteers), also describes the problem in detail, as well as presenting some ideas for addressing it.

title: Converting OSM layers into point-only GeoJSON for ODK
body:
# Converting OSM layers with points and polygons into point-only GeoJSON for ODK

ODK Collect, at this moment, only allows `Select_one_from_file` (select from map) from point-only layers. Therefore if a layer of features to be tagged, such as buildings, contains mainly polygons, it is necessary to convert those polygons into centroids to make them available to ODK Collect users.

This is really trivial in QGIS (just use the `Vector` -> `Geometry tools` -> `Centroids` tool), but in PyGDAL it turns out to be rather complicated and messy; [the default solution ](https://www.giserdqy.com/ogr/30345/#Save_centroids_of_input_Layer_to_an_output_Layer) seems to involve a lot of iteration to copy over attributes, when all we nominally want is to replace the polygon geometry with point geometry.

There are a lot of ways to attack this problem, and probably many of them would be fine, but we do need to simply pick one and go with it. I'm guessing the most straightforward option will be to use [PostGIS's ST_Centroid](https://postgis.net/docs/ST_Centroid.html) function; we already plan to have the geometry in PostGIS so manipulating it with PostGIS's native tools seems sensible.

Otherwise, implementing the disgusting iterated solution above would probably work.

title: Provide Submissions as OSM XML, GeoJSON, and/or CSV for Validation with JOSM, QGIS, or a spreadsheet
body:
When a task (which, we remember, corresponds to a form in ODK) is complete and marked "Ready for validation," the validator is most likely to wish to view the results in:

- JOSM, therefore OSM XML
- QGIS or some other GIS software, therefore GeoJSON
- A spreadsheet, therefore CSV (or possibly .xlsx)

The most likely path here is:

- Validator (who is logged in as a validator on a PC, not as a mapper on a phone) clicks on a square marked "Ready for validation."
- They see a popup offering them a few options:
  - Open in JOSM (which mirrors the process that the HOT Tasking manager uses; it launches JOSM with the OSM XML open)
  - Download OSM XML
  - Download GeoJSON
  - Download CSV
  - Download all assets (probably a ZIP file with the OSM XML, GeoJSON, and CSV bundled together)

Once the validator has the data in their hands, we have no further responsibilities toward them other than to allow them to mark the relevant square "Complete and validated". It might also make sense to add a status for "and also uploaded to OSM".

title: Choose from a library of ODK XLSForms for OSM field mapping
body:
When a Campaign Manager creates a project, they basically select three parameters:

1. An Area of Interest
2. A task-splitting strategy
3. A data model/questionnaire

Here we're focusing on 3, the data model/questionnaire, which is implemented as an [ODK XLSForm](https://xlsform.org/). We should provide a library of basic, common, high-quality XLSForms that cover many OSM field mapping scenarios. 

Those forms should incorporate standard, valid, community-accepted tags, as well as the data models being developed by HOT's Data Team.

They should be accompanied by YAML files allowing @robsavoye 's odkconvert (specifically the [osmdump module](https://github.com/hotosm/odkconvert/blob/main/ODKDump.py) to convert the resulting submissions smoothly into OSM XML.

When a Campaign Manager creates a project, they should be able to choose from this library of forms. 

Some (well, many) Campaign Managers will need to modify forms to collect data specific to their project. That's the subject of another issue, #10!

title: Option to modify XLSForms
body:
Campaign Managers often need to collect data specific to their project, context, client, or community. It's impossible to cover all eventual needs in a library of XLSForms. Therefore we will need to allow people to create or modify their own XLSForms to collect the data they need.

At the moment, it's quite straightforward to create a project with any XLSForm; as long as the form adheres to a specific structure:
- The `select_one_from_file` question _must_ be row 9 of the `survey` tab
- The `form_title` and `form_id` _must_ be row 2 (cell A2 and B2 respectively) of the `settings` tab

If the forms adhere to these constraints, the FMTM tools can already ingest them an link them to geography files for individual tasks. We just need a way to allow users to upload them. For example, when persuing the library of forms (see issue #9), the user should probably have the option to "Upload my own XLSForm", and ideally also download one of the forms from the library to modify and re-upload (with some checks to make sure the name and ID are appropriately changed).

title: Task status list
body:
# A set of status tags for task areas

Each task (area) must have a status. This is similar to (and basically aligned with) the HOT TM setup, which has a set of statuses associated with display colors:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5991943/197854202-c9c1530e-aedf-4c71-905a-498e6d5edcf5.png)

The back end will maintain a table of tasks with a status column. The API will provide the table to the client(s), including codes for the pre-defined statuses.

# The immediately-needed statuses are:
- Available for mapping
- Checked out (not available)
- Ready for Validation
- Passed Validation
- Failed Validation

### Available for mapping
The task is available for anyone to select. Usually this means it hasn't been touched by anyone else.
### Checked out
Someone has selected the task and is presumably working on it; no one else is able to select it.
### Ready for Validation
The mapper who checked out the task has completed it to their own satisfaction, and is indicating that they are ready for it to be reviewed by a validator. That mapper can now select another task.
### Passed Validation
A validator has reviewed the task and indicated that it is of sufficient quality for inclusion in the final outputs. In some cases the validator may have fixed minor errors (spelling, capitalization, or other minor issues). Generally this status means the data will be uploaded to OSM and/or the final data products from the project. 
### Failed Validation
A validator has reviewed the task and found that something is wrong, missing, or otherwise insufficient. For now, this doesn't include any further comments; the validator will need to contact the mapper or Campaign Manager to discuss remedies; usually the original mapper needs to go back and fix the problem, or another mapper needs to take over. 

In the future, we may include a mechanism for validators to provide direct feedback on the quality via the FMTM, and perhaps other ways to re-open the task in such a way that *only the original mapper or another selected person can access it*.

title: Create Project via zip upload
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A user must be able to upload a project. For the initial beta, this upload should be in the format of a .zip file, containing the following:
- `[PROJECT_NAME_PREFIX].geojson` containing the outline geometry of the project
- `[PROJECT_NAME_PREFIX]_polygons.geojson` containing the outline geometries of every task in the project. Each task should be a feature that includes a "fid": the id of this task in the project, "NUMPOINTS": representing the number of features in this task, and "task": containing the task name that is associated with the qrcode and geojson (example for uid:1, task:"0001")
- a directory named `QR_codes` with a qrcode for each task with the name formatted: `[PROJECT_NAME_PREFIX]_[TASK_TYPE_PREFIX]__[TASK_NAME].png` for example `Naivasha_buildings__0001.png`
- a directory named `geojson` with a geojson file for each task with all relevant features for that task area (for example all the buildings), with the name formatted: `[PROJECT_NAME_PREFIX]_[TASK_TYPE_PREFIX]__[TASK_NAME].geojson` for example `Naivasha_buildings__0001.geojson`

**Describe the solution you'd like**
To complete this feature there will need to be a way to create an initial project with an initial project info.

There should also be a route that takes a [PROJECT_ID], a [PROJECT_NAME_PREFIX], a [TASK_TYPE_PREFIX] and a zipfile. This endpoint should verify the zip file contains all the necessary files, create the project and tasks in the database, and return the project. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Eventually a project should be able to be created and configured in a ui, modularly, rather than through a zip upload.

title: Basic dumb polygonization of tasks from OSM lines
body:
Campaign Managers need to be able to define an AOI and get it chopped up into individual tasks. 

In the long run, we need this to be a powerful and flexible solution capable of delivering different results based on different contexts and task types; the plan is to institute a "feature bounty" for communities to contribute to this as described in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wWu8WkRmFokO5naskexvTfUOiTfULv6Rz3-3O2g6KA0/edit?usp=sharing). However, in the meantime, we need to simply get the scaffolding up and a basic version of task-splitting working (in full recognition that this will, for most campaigns, require additional manual splitting but at least creates a starting point.

We have a manual algorithm using QGIS that can be automated, ideally all in PostGIS, but anything fully automated is fine. Here is a description of the algorithm in QGIS:

## Create the polygons
- The Campaign Manager creates a single polygon for the entire Area of Interest of the project.
  -  This can be done in QGIS, and we can easily implement it in Leaflet for a Web interface, as [per the example here of a tile scraper](https://github.com/HumanitarianStuff/tilehuria-flask) that allows users to define an AOI in a browser ([live demo at turkus.net](https://turkus.net/) at time of writing) but for now just assume Campaign Managers can create an AOI polygon in QGIS.
- Download all line features from OSM. This will mostly be a bunch of roads, waterways, and railways. We'll use these as cutlines.
- Turn the AOI polygon into a line. In QGIS this is `Vector` -> `Geometry Tools` -> `Polygons to Lines`. The line will still describe a polygon, but it'll be treated by the GIS system as a line whose start and end happen to be the same, which allows it to be merged with the layer of OSM lines (you can't merge lines with polygons directly).
- Merge the AOI polygon layer with the OSM line layer. In QGIS this is `Vector` -> `Data Management Tools` -> `Merge Vector Layers`. This produces a new line layer with both components.
  - In the future, this is a point at which we'll want to do a lot more to make these polygons sane and appropriate for field mapping. However, that's a task for later; either the Algorithm bounty mentioned above, or a separate development phase.
- Create polygons of all areas enclosed by the lines in the new layer. This is a bit like the old MS Paint bucket algorithm, which fills any area completely surrounded by lines. In QGIS, we open `Processing` -> `Toolbox, search the resulting pane with `polygonize` (found in `Vector Geometry` in the toolbox). Run the merged vector layer of the AOI and OSM lines through it (no need to check the `keep table structure of line layer` box), which produces a layer called `Polygons`.
- Save the polygon layer as a GeoPackage, because we need a unique ID for each polygon (saving it as a PostGIS layer will also do this; it doesn't matter how you get a UID for each enclosed polygon), but in QGIS saving it as a GPKG works well.
- Good idea to convert the UIDs into padded strings, like `1` becomes `0001` and so on. In QGIS, this can be done in the Field Calculator using the `lpad` function.
- Now you have a polygon layer. It's unlikely to be sufficiently evenly divided for sensible tasking, but it's a start, and can be refined from there either manually or with our eventual automated solution.

## Get the features and split them by task
- Download whatever features you're planning to digitize. If they're point features like most nodes labelled "Amenity" in OSM, good enough. If they're polygon (or even line) features, for the moment we need to convert them into centroids to work with ODK's Select from Map functionality. In QGIS  this is `Vector` -> `Geometry tools` -> `Centroids`.
- Join the UIDs from the polygon layer using `Vector` -> `Data Management Tools` -> `Join Attributes by Location`. This will add a column to the centroid layer, such that every centroid has a field corresponding to that of the task polygon it falls within.
  - There's some complexity around naming this column that I'll explain later, which relates to how the FMTM back end processes the tasks
- Split the centroids into multiple GeoJSON files using `Vector` -> `Data Management Tools` -> `Split Vector Layer`. Select the GeoJSON output format, and create a directory to contain the multiple files. It'll create one file per set of features in each polygon.

title: Unzip, collate submissions, expand geopoints
body:
The dl-submissions module now:
- Unzips submissions from each form, 
- checks for CSV with more than a header row
- checks for an ODK GeoPoint-type column, expands it into 4 additional columns for easy import into QGIS or direct conversion to GIS files like GeoJSON
- Writes the individual CSV files to a specified directory (not in a Zip archive)
- Writes a collated CSV for the entire project
  - WARNING: this will probably do something horrible if there are different types of surveys in a project; it's only sensible at the moment if it's a single survey split amongst multiple geographies (as we're basically doing now with the FMTM)
- If any media attachments, creates the subdirectory specified in the Zip archive for them and writes them (again outside of the archive). 

## TODO:
- The collation and geopoint expansion happen automatically, should be flags to do or not.
- The function to simply download and write the Zip archives exists but is not accessible (again should be a flag, i.e. -z or whatever)
- The geopoint expansion _will_ go wrong with multiple survey types in a single project

title: Format codebase using pre-commit hooks (black, ruff)
body:
**This PR is entirely formatting related - no code was edited**

- In a previous PR I added a pre-commit config for pre-commit hooks. To use:
```bash
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```
Then all of the files in any commit you make will have the hooks ran on them (formatted, linted, sorted) automatically, prior to committing.

- In this PR I ran black against all Python code, prettier for markdown and yaml files.
- The goal was to have a fully formatted base to start editing from, as we don't want to muddy commits with formatting old code further down the line.
- Everything apart from src/frontend was formatted (as I don't want to cause merge conflicts with those working on the frontend).

title: Add an empty line after every file with code
body:
**Add an empty line after every file with code**

There are several reasons why this convention is followed:

1. Some programming languages and tools require the last line of a file to end with a newline character. Not having a newline character at the end of a file can cause issues when working with these tools.

2. The newline character is used as a delimiter to separate lines of code in a file. If the last line of a file doesn't end with a newline character, it can sometimes cause issues when concatenating files or processing them in other ways.

3. It can also make the file more readable, especially when working with text editors or command-line tools that display files. Having an empty line at the end of a file can make it easier to visually distinguish the end of the file from the last line of code.

cc @spwoodcock @petya-kangalova @robsavoye

title: Semantic versioning for backend and frontend
body:
We should have semantic versioning for our app.

https://semver.org/
major.minor.patch
x.x.x

We could do this, along with automatic changelogs, via conventional commit messages https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/ and using Commitizen https://commitizen-tools.github.io/commitizen (integrated with PDM).

This would also enable version tagging and version releases via GitLab.

While easy to implement for the backend API, it is tricky to include the frontend in the same repo. A monorepo setup does not lend itself to easy version control, so we may need to revisit this in future.

I propose we start with version control for the backend only, as an alpha release.

Setup development server
body: To help keep the fmtm.hotosm.org server more stable for both demos, we need a development server that can be abused. Since FMTM creates thousands of tasks and data extracts, it can quickly be overwhelming to navigate via ODK Central. The dev server should run the unstable backend from the development branch and ODK Central. Restarting ODK Central's docker container will clean the database to reduce the mess. While users of FMTM will never look at the ODK Central server at all, during development it's necessary to make sure all the XForms and data extracts are actually being uploaded.

title: Implement Create Project webpage

Now that the FMTM backend can work with ODK Central, this task creates projects without using a zip file. This new page will allow the project manager to create a project in both FMTM and ODK Central. Creating a project requires a description,instructions, the project boundary, and the type of mapping campaign.

Once this is created, the FMTM backend will create all the QR-codes, the XForm, appusers, and data extracts, and upload all of that to ODK Central. Optionally it will create a satellite imagery basemap for ODK Collect if desired, although that could take several hours to download map tiles into the cache.

title: Use odk_merge.py to process submissions
body: As part of the post mapping process, the FMTM backend needs to convert the CSV submissions from ODK Central, convert them to OSM, and then use odk_merge to conflate the new data with existing OSM data. This will use the data extract, downloaded from ODK Central for existing OSM data for conflation. The result is an OSM file with the new edited tags merged with existing tags. This file when loaded into JOSM and using the JOSM "updated modified" will then allow the new data to be uploaded to OSM after brief validation.

title: Use the Underpass raw OSM database
body: Currently data extracts expect to use a local postgres database with all the data in it. This does not scale. Since HOT maintains a raw OSM database updated every minute, data extracts should come from that database, as it contains the entire planet. The raw database support a REST API that uses a YAML config file to create the SQL query. Currently the make_data_extract.y program has the SQL queries, so this change it to query our remote database, instead of a local one.

title: Implement support for roles in the backend
body:
Currently the database and backend has no support for roles, so this will need to be added. The initial roles would be these:

Based on the experience in Dominica, I suspect we'll need the following roles:

- **Admin** (all permissions for everything on the server)
- **Group (Organisation) Admin** (all permissions within a group, so they can create, edit, process, or delete projects for their own agency, but not see or mess with projects by another group; so for example the Red Cross admin can do everything with the Red Cross' projects but not see or mess with Save the Children's projects)
- **Field Admin** (cannot create projects, but can unlock tasks unilaterally—we saw the need for this during the Dominica mapping when mappers locked tasks, didn't map them, and no one other than the mapper who locked them could force-unlock them to access the QR codes)
- **Field Mapper** (select tasks and mark them complete)
- **Validator** (select tasks, download the submissions, mark them validated or rejected)

title: Create staging deployment workflow using generic docker setup
body:
### Currently we have
- A local development setup, by using the docker-compose.yml and a .env.
- A development server: currently this uses docker-compose.prod.yml with some hardcoded/tweaked variables on the server. @mahesh-naxa has more details on this.
  - Ideally we should deploy this in the same way as prod, by using the checked out repo branch, instead of a repo that is located on the server itself (preventing file permission conflicts, or git conflicts during pull of the `development` branch.
- A production server: which uses docker-compose.prod.yml, including some hardcoded values (domains) in the compose file.

### Proposed setup
- Keep the local development `docker-compose.yml` as it is - works nicely.
- Three separate docker-compose files/configs (required for now to hardcode domain names for traefik)
  - `deploy/docker-compose.dev.yml` (excludes local ODKCentral, uses a standalone version for testing)
  - `deploy/docker-compose.stag.yml` (includes local ODKCentral)
  - `deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml` (includes local ODKCentral)
- Each config will have an environment set on Github, including a secret .env variable that is injected on deploy.
- Each config will have a Github action associated for the deploy (they should be identical, just with different secrets).
- Each config should use it's own image tags. E.g. fmtm:main, fmtm:development, fmtm:staging

### Prerequisite
- Create a staging branch in the repo.

### Note
- The traefik setup currently blocks us creating a generic docker-compose for deployment (regex to remove `https://` doesn't work).
- We may be able to simplify this setup by changing API_URL, FRONTEND_MAIN_URL, FRONTEND_MAP_URL to API_DOMAIN, FRONTEND_MAIN_DOMAIN, FRONTEND_MAP_DOMAIN (forgotten if I already tried this & was blocked by something...).
- The domain vars can then be used for traefik variable injection and `http://` or `https://` prepended to their use requiring the protocol. We could also create a FRONTEND_PROTOCOL variable to specify and inject `http`:// or `https`://.
- This would result in:
`docker-compose.yml` local dev
`docker-compose.deploy.yml` for staging and prod, with env var injection
`docker-compose.noodk.yml` for dev deploy, with env var injection (remove all odkcentral services)

title: Add expand xlsforms table
body:
Currently the backend assumes the category is the same as the XLSForm filename. This may not always be the case. Over time, some categories might have multiple related XLSForms, If a category column is added, it would be possible to support the times when the XLSForm filename conflicts with an OSM tag that is used in the XLSForm. In addition to adding the category column, a filespec should be added that refer to the actual XLSForm source file. While for now the title is the same as  the filespec, it should be changed to be a more descriptive title. When uploading a custom XLSForm, the mapper will need to specify both the title and the category.

There is a new function make_data_extract.py:getChoices() which reads in the new config file that maps XLSForm filenames to a category. This returns a dict(). Any place in src/backend that refers to the XLSForm needs to get the value based on the category. For example, PostgresClient() takes an optional argument for the cases the XLSForm name is not the same as the category.

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we manage backend dependencies manually, using a requirements.txt file.

This doesn't lend itself to easy updates in the future.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should use a dependency solving tool, such as poetry or PDM.

I propose PDM, as it's very fast, has full pyproject.toml support, and is simple to use with both venv and PEP582.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Poetry is good too.
Pipenv is too slow at dependency solving.

title: Support multiple Form formats
body: Currently the frontend asks to upload an XForm, but expects an .xlsx file. This should support both .xls and .xlsx format for custom XLSForm definitions. This assume it'll be converted on the server side. This should also allow for an .xml file that doesn't need to be converted.

title: Custom data extracts alongside custom XLSForm
body:
osm-fieldwork uses osm-rawdata to generate data extracts.
The `data_models/*.yaml` files define the SQL query that will be used.

Right now a custom XLSForm needs to be mapped to one of the existing data models (categories).

This works fine for a standard XLSForm, however, if we upload a custom XLSForm we need to also be able to specify a custom SQL query to get the data extract we want.

To facilitate this we need to be able to upload a `.yaml` file defining the SQL query alongside out custom XLSForm.

To do this we need:
- Backend: to pass the yaml config file to PostgresClient in osm-rawdata.
- Frontend: UI component to generate the yaml for a project (better UX).

The generated yaml is stored in the `project.form_config_file` table, then passed to osm-rawdata when generating the extract.

title: Improve Handling of System Outages with Graceful Error Pages
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Yes, the feature request is related to handling system outages gracefully. When the backend of a platform is down, it is important to provide a user-friendly and informative error page instead of leaving users confused or frustrated.

Right now, when the backend API had an outage, the UI loaded but could not perform any 1) form submit actions. 2) fetching projects 3) fetching organization 

![image](https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/assets/11831955/0a870fc6-7a2e-4721-bc91-cde2a19dca75)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like the platform to display a well-designed error page when the backend or frontend is experiencing an outage. The error page should clearly convey that there is a temporary issue with the system and provide relevant information to the users. It should include a friendly message explaining the situation, perhaps an apology for the inconvenience caused, and any additional details that might be helpful.

Additionally, the error page could include relevant links or contact information for support, so users can report the issue or seek further assistance if needed. It should be designed in a visually appealing manner, consistent with the overall branding and user experience of the platform.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative solution could be redirecting users to a generic error page or simply displaying a generic error message without any additional information.

title: Organisations
Modification of AOI Splits: Enhancing AOI Split and Feature Set Management with Download and Upload Functionality
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Users currently do not have a straightforward way to obtain copies of the AOI split and feature set artifacts generated by the FMTM system. This lack of download functionality restricts users from accessing and utilizing these artifacts outside of the FMTM system. Additionally, users are unable to upload modified versions of the AOI split and feature set, limiting their ability to make customized adjustments.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Enable users to upload modified versions of the AOI split and feature set.
2. Provide the AOI split as a downloadable GeoJSON file and the feature set as a separate file format (e.g., CSV, GeoJSON).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative approach would be to develop an in-app editing tool within the FMTM system. However, implementing a full-fledged editing tool can be complex and time-consuming. By providing download and upload functionality, users can leverage existing external tools, such as QGIS, which are widely used and provide robust editing capabilities. This approach allows users to work with familiar tools and workflows while reducing the development effort required for an in-app editing feature.

title: Improved Auto-Fill for ODK Central URL and Username Fields
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Entering the ODK Central URL and username every time when accessing the FMTM platform can be inconvenient and time-consuming. This repetitive task becomes a hassle for users who frequently use the platform.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Instead of building a new feature within the FMTM platform, I propose leveraging the auto-fill option provided by web browsers. The desired solution includes the following:

1. Enable auto-fill for the ODK Central URL field: When users start typing the URL, the browser should suggest previously used URLs based on the user's browsing history. This feature saves time by eliminating the need to manually enter the complete URL every time.

Example:
In most browsers, you can make your browser display values previously entered in input fields by giving a name to the input. For example:

```html
<input type="text" id="centralURL" placeholder="ODK Central URL" name="centralURL">
```

2. Enable auto-fill for the ODK username field: Similar to the URL field, the browser should remember the username previously entered by the user. As the user starts typing, the browser should suggest and auto-fill the username based on past entries, saving time and effort.

Example:
It may vary depending on the browser and user privacy settings and sorts, and it should be on by default, but try adding `autocomplete="on"` to your input tag.

```html
<input type="text" id="username" placeholder="Username" name="username" autocomplete="on">
```

By enabling the auto-fill functionality of the browser for these two fields, users can easily access the FMTM platform without the hassle of typing the ODK Central URL and username repeatedly.

Reference: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/16444496/make-text-input-fields-remember-previously-entered-data 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative approach would be to include a "Remember Me" checkbox or a "Save Login Credentials" option within the FMTM platform itself. However, leveraging the auto-fill feature provided by web browsers is a widely-used and established method that users are already familiar with. This approach also eliminates the need for additional development work on the FMTM platform.

Real-time Task Locking Status Update in Map
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, when a task is locked by another user in the mapping application, the locked status is not automatically reflected in real-time for other users. They need to manually refresh the page to see the updated status. This can lead to conflicts and errors when multiple users try to lock the same task simultaneously, resulting in a "Failed to update task" error message.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to have a real-time update of the locked status in the mapping application, so that when a task is locked by another user, it is immediately reflected for all other users without the need to manually refresh the page. This would provide a seamless and efficient experience for users and help prevent conflicts and errors.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One alternative solution could be implementing a periodic polling mechanism where the application checks for updates at regular intervals. However, this approach may introduce unnecessary network traffic and latency.

title: Enhancing Page Titles in Browser Tabs
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, all pages in the mapping application have the same title of "fmtm" displayed in the browser tab. This lack of specific page titles can confuse and frustrate users, especially those who utilize multiple tabs in their web browsers. When users have multiple tabs open from the mapping application, it becomes challenging to identify and locate the desired tab quickly. This inconsistency in tab titles hinders the user experience and makes it harder for power users to manage their workflows efficiently.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to improve the user experience by providing more informative and context-specific page titles for each page in the mapping application. By incorporating meaningful titles, users can easily distinguish between different tabs and identify the purpose of each tab at a glance. The desired format for the page titles is as follows:

1. Explore Projects: "Explore Projects - HOT Field Mapping And Tasking Manager"
2. Manage Organization: "Manage Organization - HOT Field Mapping And Tasking Manager"
3. Login: "Login - HOT Field Mapping And Tasking Manager"
4. Project Name: "Project Name - HOT Field Mapping And Tasking Manager" (Here, the task name dynamically changes based on the project being accessed)

By having clear and distinct page titles, power users who frequently utilize multiple tabs will have a more streamlined and organized browsing experience, allowing them to locate and switch between tabs with ease.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One alternative solution could be to have a generic page title format for all pages, such as "HOT - Field Mapping And Tasking Manager" However, this would not provide specific information about the purpose of each page or the project/task being accessed, which can be valuable for users.

title: Improving contribution guidelines
body:
1. **Tagging "Good First Issue"**: To encourage new contributors, it's helpful to add a "good first issue" tag to tasks that are relatively easy to complete. These issues should be well-defined and require minimal prior knowledge of the project.

2. **Submitting a Pull Request (Server and Client Components)**:
   - Provide step-by-step instructions on how to fork the repository.
   - Explain how to clone the forked repository locally.
   - Detail the process of creating a new branch for the proposed changes.
   - Describe how to make the necessary changes and test them locally.
   - Explain the process of pushing the changes to the forked repository.
   - Instruct contributors on how to submit a pull request from their forked repository to the main repository.
   - Emphasize the importance of providing a clear description of the changes made in the pull request.

3. **Code Style Guides Document**: It's crucial to maintain a consistent code style throughout the project. Include a document or a reference to an existing code style guide that outlines the preferred coding conventions, formatting, and best practices for the server and client components. This will help contributors align their code with the project's standards.

4. **Work in Progress Pull Requests**: Encourage contributors to mark their pull requests as "work in progress" if they are still developing or refining the changes. This helps prevent premature merging and allows for early feedback from maintainers and other contributors.

5. **Review Process**: Outline the review process for pull requests, including expectations for maintainers and contributors. Explain how feedback will be provided, and encourage contributors to actively participate in discussions and address feedback promptly.

6. **Code of Conduct**: Include a code of conduct that sets the expectations for respectful and inclusive behavior within the community. Provide information on how to report violations and ensure that all contributors adhere to the code of conduct.

Imagery basemaps are very useful in the field when the map data isn't very complete. Osm-fieldwork has a **basemapper.py** program which downloads map tiles from several different sources. It creates an XYZ map tile store on disk, and using a boundary polygon, extracts the tiles that fit in that boundary. It can write both .mbtiles for ODK Collect, and sqlitedb files for Osmand. Both output formats should be supported.

**EDIT** mbtiles have been implemented. We still need mbtile and pmtile at some point.

Optimise PWA for low connectivity environments
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
- FMTM may be used in areas of poor connectivity.
- Ideally it should still work well if the connection is intermittent.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Creating a manifest and service worker config file should make this a PWA (that can also be installed as an app, improving UX).
- A few caching options will be available for GET requests, keeping a subset of features available even if connectivity drops.
- Perhaps a banner should be displayed indicating the user is offline.
- Caching of POST requests may also be possible, deferring the sending of data until connection is restored.
- We could even go so far as to cache all tasks in IndexDB via something like Dexie.

**Additional context**
- A field campaign recently experienced issues with low connectivity.
- Loading the app before going to an area with no internet would be required.
- Caching tasks via IndexDB would also reduce load on the API. We would have to check there are no performance implications for users with older phone models and weigh up what is best.

title: Implement OpenTelemetry for tracing, logging, metrics
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
- We need a way to monitor FMTM, especially when being used actively in the field.
- Performance and downtime monitoring.
- Tracing of the entire request chain, from frontend --> backend --> database and back.
- Record logging from the application server.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Two options:
- Open-source Sentry replacements such as GlitchTip.
- Open-telemetry based solutions (my preference).

Historically observability tools are either closed source or their own open-source implementation of something.
open-telemetry aims to standardise traces, logs, metrics: https://opentelemetry.io/
Instrumentation is available for frontend JS, backend Python.

The idea is that you can generate JSON based traces, transmitted efficiently using protobuf or gRPC.
A backend server accepts these traces and stores in e.g. clickhouse.
A frontend tool can view the traces nicely, e.g. SigNoz.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
GlitchTip may be worth considering too, but only for application logging.
It would have less information, but we should assess if it's more lightweight.

**Additional context**
We don't want to interfere with the main data being transmitted.
The traces/logs/metrics should be very lightweight, particularly in places with limited internet connectivity.

title: Add JOSM API to docker compose dev stack
body:
Part misunderstanding, part fun little project.

I originally containerised JOSM in the hope to make the API accessible.

**Two Issues**

- JOSM is useless without the GUI component.

- JOSM has very strict and non-configurable remote access settings. It's accessible on 127.0.0.1:8111, which doesn't work with Docker (uses localhost).

**Solution**

- I made the JOSM GUI accessible via noVNC. This way we don't need to install Java or JOSM on our local machine for development. It runs entirely in a container, the GUI accessible on `localhost:8112`.

- I added nginx to the JOSM container, which is against the one-service-per-container ethos, but necessary in this case. Nginx reverse-proxies 127.0.0.1:8111 to localhost:80, making the JOSM API accessible by port mapping the container 8111:8111. Now we have remote JOSM available on `localhost:8111` for development.

**Next Steps**

- Tasking manager connects remotely to the JOSM API and configures the user session.
- It doesn't use anything fancy: just http calls using URL params.
- We can do the same from the FMTM frontend (making calls from the backend if needed too using `josm:80`).
- E.g. we can call a URL like: `http://127.0.0.1:8111/load_and_zoom?left=8.19&right=8.20&top=48.605&bottom=48.590&select=node413602999` to configure JOSM remotely.

**Note:** I added docs on how to run this in DEV-2: Backend.

title: Remove manual signup/login (use OSM)
body:
## Issues

**1**
We want to use OSM login for everything.
Manual login is a legacy feature we used before getting OSM login working.

**2**
Currently we default to OAUTHLIB_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=1 in the backend, which is insecure and could leak user credentials.

**3**
OSM login does not work during development, only production.

## Solution

- Removed login and signup code from frontend.
- Removed API endpoints for login and signup.
- Default to OSM login only during dev/prod.
- Update docs with OSM redirect url info for frontend.
- Remove default OAUTHLIB_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=True in backend & only set this if DEBUG=True.

Within this PR I also updated the OSM OAuth login flow slightly via the frontend.
It worked in production, but produced CORS errors during development.
I updated to use window.postMessage for secure communication between the popup and main window.
Now we can use OSM login during development / testing too.

## Additional Context

With the current setup, if a user attempt OSM login, but there is a manual user with the same name, then we get an error.

@nrjadkry is working on a migration for manual users, so we can keep them in dev/prod for the time being.

The login for dev/prod already defaults to OSM, so if any user finds themself locked out of manual login, they can contact us & we will migrate their entries to an OSM account user.
(this was the main concern of Ivan - not locking out any existing users)

title: Store encrypted ODK credentials in database
body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently ODK credentials, particularly the password, are stored as plain text in the database.

**Solution**
They should probably be encrypted.
It's generally bad security practice to decrypt passwords (they should be hashed, salted, peppered), but it's probably necessary in our case.

**Example**

```python
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
import base64

from app.config import settings

cipher_suite = Fernet(settings.ENCRYPTION_KEY)

def encrypt_password(password: str) -> str:
    encrypted_password = cipher_suite.encrypt(password.encode())
    return base64.b64encode(encrypted_password).decode("utf-8")

def decrypt_password(encrypted_password: str) -> str:
    encrypted_password = base64.b64decode(encrypted_password.encode())
    decrypted_password = cipher_suite.decrypt(encrypted_password)
    return decrypted_password.decode("utf-8")

password_to_store = "mysecretpassword"
encrypted_password = encrypt_password(password_to_store)
print("Encrypted Password:", encrypted_password)

decrypted_password = decrypt_password(encrypted_password)
print("Decrypted Password:", decrypted_password)
```

This isn't ideal, but would be better than what we have now.
(more thought required to make this better)

Use pre-commit.ci for code quality checks
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently we have a pre-commit configuration, which can be used to auto format, lint, and quality control code.

The idea is that the developer installs a pre-commit hook (`pre-commit install`) that triggers when a commit attempt is made, running and preventing succesful commit until fixes are made.

The issue is that it's entirely optional / not enforceable.


**Describe the solution you'd like**

[Pre-commit.ci](https://pre-commit.ci/) is a new tool built around GitHub actions.

It makes pre-commit run automatically during push or PR, so that the developer is prompted to fix any errors before the PR is merged.

This should:
- Prevent the occurrence of mistakes in PRs, but picking up basic errors.
- Keep coding style consistent across the entire codebase.

In their own words:
"""
Developers spend a fair chunk of time during their development flow on fixing relatively trivial problems in their code. pre-commit.ci both enforces that these issues are discovered (which is opt-in for each developer's workflow via pre-commit) but also fixes the issues automatically, letting developers focus their time on more valuable problems.
"""


**Additional context**

Reviewing PRs can be time consuming when formatting changes are also included in the Git diff. This solution should solve that problem.

It's entirely free to use for open-source repos.

title: Update logging to be more feature rich, persist logs, JSON logs
body:
## Issue

- Currently we use logging.basicConfig, which is fine, but not very configurable.
- Logs also don't currently persist after container restarts, which doesn't help debugging if multiple PRs and merged in succession (redeploy).

## Solution

I updated to use the loguru library, which is very feature rich and easy to use.

The setup:
- Log to terminal in a standardised way, hooking all downstream loggers.
- Add colour to logs if your terminal supports it.
- All log calls are non-blocking, using multithreading.
- Backtracing for more detailed logs on traceback.
- Generic error catching, so if an unhandled exception occurs, the server doesn't go down.
- Logging to rotating files in JSON format, located in a docker volume (these logs could be synced to S3 in the future and easily ingested / analysed on a dashboard).

## Notes

I made this PR after having to debug something - hopefully this makes it easier.

title: Update deploy config to use multiple vars
body:
Currently we use a single DOTENV variable, which was flexible during rapid development, but not be ideal going forward.

As FMTM var config is relatively stable now, we should divide into separate environment variables, or environment secrets if sensitive config.

Advantages:

- Easier updating of individual variables.
- Different teams can manage different vars, e.g. some managed by DevOps.
- We can use variables from a secrets management system. Especially if we migrate to cloud based solutions.

title: Use WebGL renderer for OpenLayers VectorLayer & VectorTileLayer
body:
## Issue

Poor performance of geojson and vector tile layers in OpenLayers.

## Solution

Relatively new WebGL renderers for OpenLayers.
- VectorLayer renderer: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/examples/webgl-vector-layer.html
- VectorTileLayer renderer: https://openlayers.org/en/latest/examples/webgl-vector-tiles.html
(ol/layer/WebGLTile is already available for raster sources)

They should be available in ol v8.
Although the API is not fully stable yet, we can accept this.
Test the renderers to see if they solve performance issues.
(if the VectorLayer renderer works nicely, we won't have to bother testing with flatgeobuf / geoparquet for now)

title: Alembic Setup
body:
**Description:**
This pull request introduces Alembic setup to our existing database configuration, enhancing our database management capabilities. Alembic is a powerful tool for database schema versioning and migration, and this addition will streamline the process of maintaining and evolving our database schema.

**Changes Made:**
Integration of Alembic into our project's database setup.
Configuration files for Alembic migrations.
Initial database migration scripts.

**Benefits:**
Improved database version control: Alembic allows us to track changes to our database schema over time, making it easier to roll back changes if necessary and maintain a consistent schema across different environments.
Simplified database migrations: Alembic automates the process of creating and applying database migrations, reducing the risk of human error during schema updates.
Enhanced collaboration: With Alembic in place, multiple team members can work on database changes concurrently, ensuring smoother collaboration and reducing conflicts.

**Todo**
1. In order to fully operationalize Alembic, we may need to set up an entry point that allows executing the following command for running migration files:
`alembic upgrade head`
2. Allow access to create migration files in the versions folder. Currently, the setup does not permit users to create new files in the versions folder

title: Add SQL-based migration script, with migration dir
body:
## Issue

- Currently we have no way of migrating new database edits on editing databases.
- We tested using `alembic`, but the setup is too complex for our needs and it's a bit of a black box.
- In the future we plan to remove SQLAlchemy anyway: #254

## Solution

I have made a migration bash script, that is bundled with the backend.

The way it works:

- SQL migration scripts are placed in the `src/backend/migrations` dir.
  - These should be idempotent, i.e. can run over and over without causing errors.
  - There should also be a commented out SQL script for how to revert the migration.
  - Scripts should be named sequentially, i.e. the first is 001-some-migration.sql, then they increment by one.
  - Example `000-remove-user-password.sql`:
  
 ```sql
-- ## Migration to remove password field from public.users (replaced with OSM OAuth)


-- ## Apply Migration
-- Start a transaction
BEGIN;
-- Drop the 'password' column if it exists
ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS public.users
DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS password;
-- Commit the transaction
COMMIT;


-- ## Revert Migration (comment above, uncomment below)
-- -- Start a transaction
-- BEGIN;
-- -- Add the 'password' column back if it doesn't exist
-- ALTER TABLE public.users
-- ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS password character varying;
-- -- Commit the transaction
-- COMMIT;
``` 

- When the docker compose stack starts, an additional container starts up and runs a bash script once.
- The script generates a *table* called `migrations`, which simply tracks the script name and execution date.
- The `migrations` *directory* is scanned for new files, and if there is no record in the database of being applied, the migration is applied.

## Note

I also lazily bundled a quick fix for the CI backend docker image build in this PR.

## tl;dr

Create a `.sql` script under `src/backend/migrations` and it will be applied when the backend next starts.

- This is an acceptable strategy if running a single container, but it does mean that container storage can fill up.
- We have no way to cache submissions https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/713
- We want to serve cloud-optimised formats if possible https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/381, then fallback to offline (downloaded) files.
- We need to easily download generated files: https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/890 https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/889

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Distributed storage via S3.
- I propose we use [Garage](https://github.com/deuxfleurs-org/garage) as a lightweight alternative to S3 as part of our software stack.
  - For development and self-hosted installs of FMTM we would use Garage.
  - For production deploys on cloud infrastructure, we would use managed S3 buckets (AWS).
  - This needs to be configurable.
- Then whenever we process a file, it should be uploaded to S3 for later retrieval (by the frontend, another container, etc).

**Additional context**

Doing this would make it much easier to deploy with something like Kubernetes.

title: Simplify deployment process: curlable bash script
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- FMTM has a few components (ODK, Postgres, Garage, Backend, Frontend).
- Orchestrating this is easy with docker-compose, but not everyone know how to use docker-compose.
- A simple one command bash script would be nicer, e.g. like docker: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com/ | sh`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- A bash script hosted at fmtm.hotosm.org/install.sh (CNAME get-fmtm.hotosm.org ?)
- The bash script should (optionally) install Docker (and docker compose) first.
- ODK Central should be set up:
  - Separate docker-compose.odk.yml (dev, staging) and docker-compose.prod.yml (prod).
  - The prod docker compose will not install Garage (use hosted S3 instead) or ODK (use prod HOT ODK).
- The user should answer a few prompts generating their `.env` variables.
- The docker images should be pulled and ran with docker-compose, depending on which environment the user selected:
  - Test: could use docker-compose.yml (local setup)
  - With ODK: docker-compose.odk.yml (use for the discussed demo-feature branches / tests, i.e. spin up publicly accessible instance with all batteries included).
    - For demo-feature branches, we could possibly also add a workflow to auto-deploy, if the user provides an SSH key for a server in advance?
  - Without ODK: docker-compose.prod.yml

The end result will be a fully working instance of FMTM for users to either test, or deploy publicly for use.

**Additional considerations**

1. It would be awesome if we can allow for the installation of FMTM alongside a mesh VPN like [headscale](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale) (an open re-implementation of Tailscale control plane). This would allow an organisation to run FMTM on an internal server, and without requiring any DNS entries or SSL certificates, use a VPN (Tailscale client on their phone/pc) with 'magic-dns' to access FMTM for mapping (e.g. via http://fmtm-server). *In summary: all someone needs is a working computer in their office and they can deploy FMTM (no certs, DNS entries, and web proxies to consider)*.

2. To facilitate this it would probably be best to run a centralised HOT-operated instance of headscale. The deployment just needs a machine and DNS entry (vpn.hotosm.org?). Headscale creates and renews the cert.

3. Some deployments may be for sensitive data collection. Point 1 would facilitate running FMTM entirely privately and securely.

Note: for OSM OAuth (login) to work we need https urls. This can be solved by either:
- headscale has implemented cert generation for magic dns by then.
- using a magic dns domain we work around this by generating let's encrypt certs.
- for reference, some other options: https://www.nango.dev/blog/oauth-redirects-on-localhost-with-https

title: Dev, staging, production setup
body:
Higher level task to track a few others.

Soon I will:

- Create HOT AWS EC2 instances for development, staging, main.
- Tweak deploy config for each branch / environment.

## Development

- 2 core, 4GB.
- Frontend via Minio static website.

## Staging

- 2 core, 4GB.
- Frontend via Minio static website.

## Main (production)

- 4 core, 8GB.
- Frontend via AWS S3 static website, plus data in AWS S3 (no Minio).

## Related tasks
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/899 ✅ 
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/838 ✅ 
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/837 ✅ 
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/786 ✅ 
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/515 ✅ 
https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/371 ✅ 

## Additional tasks
- Rename FRONTEND_MAIN_URL variable to FRONTEND_URL (requires update to all .env files). ✅ 
- Change frontend config to bind the ports provided from .env file (reducing manual configuration in docker-compose.yml (requires splitting of URL into PORT and URL params). ✅ 
- **Important: don't forget to change file ownership in production deployment from UID 900 --> 1001**

## Final domains


### Production
fmtm.hotosm.org
api.fmtm.hotosm.org
s3.fmtm.hotosm.org
odk.hotosm.org (global HOTOSM instance)

### Staging
stage.fmtm.hotosm.org
api.stage.fmtm.hotosm.org
s3.stage.fmtm.hotosm.org
odk.stage.fmtm.hotosm.org

### Development
dev.fmtm.hotosm.org
api.dev.fmtm.hotosm.org
s3.dev.fmtm.hotosm.org
odk.dev.fmtm.hotosm.org

### EC2 Setup Steps:
- Create keypair in AWS console for your user account (for connecting to EC2 instances).
- Create all networking first: VPCs, subnets, route tables, internet gateways + security group (for public & private.
- Create Debian EC2 instance attached to VPC, t2.medium, auto assign public IPs, select security group, 100GB gp3 storage, 
- Log in using keypair (admin@ip for debian), install machinectl & create user svcfmtm (uid 1001):

```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y systemd-container --no-install-recommends
sudo useradd -u 1001 -m -c "fmtm account" -d /home/svcfmtm -s /bin/bash svcfmtm
# Temp add to sudoers
echo "svcfmtm ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/fmtm-sudoers >/dev/null
```

- Create keypair for user svcfmtm

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519
# name it svcfmtm
# no passphrase
# save svcfmtm and delete from the system
# scp admin@stage.fmtm.hotosm.org:/home/admin/svcfmtm .
sudo mkdir /home/svcfmtm/.ssh
sudo mv svcfmtm.pub /home/svcfmtm/.ssh/authorized_keys
sudo chown -R svcfmtm:svcfmtm /home/svcfmtm
sudo chmod 700 /home/svcfmtm/.ssh
sudo chmod 600 /home/svcfmtm/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

- Login as svcfmtm via ssh in another terminal

- Install docker with first part of install script:

```bash
curl -L https://get.fmtm.dev -o install.sh
bash install.sh
```

- Log back in as admin account & remove user from sudoers: `sudo rm /etc/sudoers.d/fmtm-sudoers`

- Add cron to prune docker images weekly (needs to use machinectl to user svcfmtm):
```bash
cd /etc/cron.weekly
sudo nano docker-prune
```
file content
```
#!/bin/bash
sudo machinectl --quiet shell \
    --setenv=DOCKER_HOST="unix:///run/user/$(id -u svcfmtm)/docker.sock" \
    svcfmtm@ /bin/bash -c "docker image prune -af"
```
then
```bash
sudo chmod +x /etc/cron.weekly/docker-prune
```

- Update shell prompt name:
  - Edit .bashrc for the user.
  - Replace `\u@\h` with `\u@fmtm-dev` (or whatever hostname you want).
  - This is in three places where PS1 is defined on Debian.

It might be good to put this in a terraform or anisible setup, under `infra`.

title: Simplify project features response & prep for flatgeobuf osm extracts
body:
# Issue

1. The response from `get_project_features_geojson` has many redundant keys, increasing the data transfer size when displaying the data extract.
2. We currently request for a data extract from raw-data-api, then download the resulting zipped geojson to /tmp, extract, and return the data. In the long run there is no need for this step. We can request a flatgeobuf file from raw-data-api, then either access directly from the S3 url (store the link in db), or upload the flatgeobuf to our own S3 for access.

# Solution

1. Simplify the returned JSON response when getting data extracts, removing keys:
```
task_id
project_id
geometry.properties.label
geometry.properties.title
geometry.properties.version
geometry.properties.changeset
geometry.properties.timestamp
```
from each JSON object in the array.

2. Update to allow passing what format we require to raw-data-api & add comment TODOs about future changes.

title: Use data extracts hosted in raw-data-api
body:
## Issue

- Currently we keep track of data extracts within the FMTM database.
- We request a data extract from raw-data-api, then input the resulting geojson data into our db.
- When we make a request for a subset of the extract (i.e. a task area), it comes from the db.
- If we need to update the data extract, we request/download again & then update the db.

## Solution

All of the above can be handled by raw-data-api:

- Request a data extract to be generated in flatgeobuf with bind_zip=False (i.e. not zipped).
- Normally the data only lasts for 90 days, but if we use a filename of `hotosm-fmtm-project-{project_id}`, the data will be persisted.
- If we request another extract for the same file, the file will be updated in place.

Essentially we remove the burden of handling data extracts ourselves, and outsource it to raw-data-api.

Tasking manager is going to do something similar.

The resulting flatgeobuf has a spatial index inbuilt and can be accessed via RANGE request, so we can subset the data for a specific task area, the same way we do now.

To do this, we pass these params via POST to the `/snapshot` endpoint:

```json
{
    "outputType": "fgb",
    "fileName": "hotosm-fmtm-project-{project_id}",
    "bindZip": false,
    "geometry": {...},
    "filters": {...}
}
```

## Additional Considerations

#### Environment

- We should also probably consider what environment we are doing this on: main, staging, development:

**main**: the filename can be `hotosm-fmtm-project-{project_id}` (will exist forever)
**staging**: the filename can be `hotosm-fmtm-staging-project-{project_id}` (will exist for undefined period, perhaps 180 days?)
**development**: the filename can be `fmtm-project-{project_id}` (will expire in 90 days with no `hotosm` prefix)

The final S3 path will be something like:

```
S3_URL/fmtm/{project_id}/hotosm-fmtm-project-{project_id}.fgb
```

#### Redundant Tables

- We can completely remove the database tables and models for managing data extracts once this refactor is complete.

- Currently we have DB tables DbOsmLines (ways) and DbBuildings.

- Do we need a flatgeobuf for each, or can we just filter in the frontend by a key? In the final parsed geojson we will have the property `building=true|false`.

title: UX: remove task info from projects/<id> endpoint, call separately
body:
## Issue

Calling the project info endpoint can take over 20 seconds if there are a lot of tasks.

E.g. https://fmtm-api.naxa.com.np/projects/24

## Solutions

- I would be best to separate the task information from the project info:
  1) On first load, the project info endpoint should be fast, returning the project outline & quickly panning to the project area on the map.
  2) The task info should be gathered from the tasks API endpoints: https://fmtm-api.naxa.com.np/tasks/task-list?project_id=24
- Coordination is required for the frontend/backend (although if the frontend part is done first, then the task info removed from the project endpoint, this wouldn't disrupt anything):

**Frontend**: change to use two API calls, one for the project, allowing the pan to project area to happen first, then load the tasks in.

**Backend**: remove the task info from the project endpoint.

## Additional Context

The tasks are loaded gradually from the API, taking most of the time receiving the response instead of waiting for it:

![image](https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/assets/78538841/477968d5-1724-487d-8fd0-1bf9bf7a135b)

Try and load the endpoint: https://fmtm-api.naxa.com.np/tasks/task-list?project_id=24
You can see the data slowly populating.

It would be interesting to see if we could populate the data on the map as it loads, instead of waiting for it all to load and displaying at the end.

title: Fix/customform uploadissue
Redesign pagination & project summaries endpoint
body:
## Original Issue

**Describe the bug**
Since we have the infinite scroll in projects page, the text displaying the range doesn't make sense. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Go to 'Explore Projects"

**Expected behavior**
Add the text "Total Projects : N" , where N = project count instead of showing n of n projects

**Screenshots**

![Image](https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/assets/108750444/0d486c27-8c5b-463f-b45c-c70a5f7a79d8)

## New Issue

- Pagination of the backend is partially addressed by: #225
- This is an approach where we can only limit the number of results, not actual pagination (?page=1, ?page=2, etc).
- We need true pagination as we grow, or the API call to fetch projects will either return too much data, or we will be unable to return data past ?limit=100.

## Proposed Solution

**Backend**

- Add pagination to the `summaries` endpoint so we can include ?page=1 syntax.
- Only return approx 13-20 project - assess what is best.
- Move the results list under the key `results`.
- Create one other top level key in the JSON called `pagination`, where pagination details are included (number of pages, total number of projects, etc).

**Frontend**

- Add `Showing x of x projects` to the home page, based of `pagination.total` key.
- Access the project summary content via the `results` key instead.

title: Revision of project creation workflow : Visibility of data extracts in the project creation workflow
body:
**Describe the bug**

I currently face the following issue with the project creation workflow:

1. I select a random form category and complete the project setup but I don't see any data extracts in tasks
2. I upload an AOI where there are no relevant data extracts, I reach the Step 5 but can't use the task splitting algorithm because there are no buildings/road data extracts
3. I can't validate the data extracts before a project is created

I would suggest the following workflow for the project setup.

_**Step 3 should include:**_

1. Selection of Feature Category (Rename Form Category to Feature Category)
2. Add a description just below the Feature Category title (Choose the feature type you want to survey)
3. The user will select from the dropdown options that we have as now.

4. Allow the user to select the type of feature category i.e. Point, Line, Polygon
5. The feature type should also be based on the feature category (For eg: If I choose buildings in feature category, I shouldn't have the option to choose line in the feature type options)
6. Now the user should be able to see the extracts as per their selection on the right side of the map
7.@nrjadkry, the backend should provide the data extracts to the frontend at this point
8. The step 7 is very important because the user should be able to validate their data extracts before they move ahead with the workflow.
9. This will also resolve the conflict where there is no relevant data extract as per the user's feature category
10 If the data extracts match the user's expectation, they move ahead, if not they can reselect the feature category 

**Note: If there are no data extracts in that AOI, the user should be displayed the message stating "There are no OSM data extracts around the AOI relevant to the feature category you chose. You may either choose to upload your custom data extracts or select a different feature category. You may still proceed ahead without any data extracts."**
 
**_Step 4 should include:_**
1. Selection of form type (Default or custom)
2. The user can either select the default form which provides the user with form relevant to form category selection
3. The user can also add custom xls forms

**_Step 5 would be the splitting of tasks as it is._**

title: Replace frontend route in proxy with AWS S3 + Cloudfront
body:
## Problem

- Currently the frontend is served from docker volume --> nginx --> user.
- This is good for development and staging environments and is more flexible for self-hosters.
- In production, this is marginally slower than other solutions. Plus egress costs may be more.

## Solution

- For the production (global) HOTOSM deployment, we should use an S3 static website, plus AWS Cloudfront to provide SSL & caching.
- This will reduce latency (S3 is spread across multiple zones), egress costs, improve caching performance.

## Implementation

- Within the ui / frontend entrypoint we already use rclone to copy to the docker volume.
- Instead rclone to the S3 bucket provided, if production.
- We probably need a variable injected into the container to determine this use case with an if block (i.e. COPY_TO_S3=True).

## Notes

- I didn't do this in the first round of devops improvements, so that I can move onto other pressing things.
- This should probably be completed before the next production deployment.

title: Add task_split_type to project when task splitting complete
body:
**Describe the bug**

- We have the database field `task_split_type` for projects.
- Three options for splitting: square, manual, or task splitting algorithm (fmtm-splitter).
- The `task_split_type` is not updated in the database after the splitting is complete.
- We have a field `splitting_algorithm` that is used in the frontend that should be renamed.

**To Reproduce**

- Create a project.
- Check the request body.
- Check the db.

**Expected behavior**

- The `task_split_type` field is updated.


## Backend Tasks

- Create an enum for `task_split_type`.
- Ensure the field is updated on project creation.

## Frontend Tasks

- Rename field `splitting_algorithm` to `task_split_type` throughout the frontend code.
- Check this is a suitable replacement in all components (`splitting_algorithm` may be used to track the component state / user selection, but the field `task_split_type` field must be included in the project creation POST request - using one of the enum options defined above).

## Additional considerations

Even if we have the `task_split_type`, we do not store the `dimension` for split on square, or the `no_of_buildings` per task for the splitting algorithm. These params would be required to reproduce a project (i.e. via an export/import).
