title: XLSForm questionaire should come after building validation questions
body:
**Describe the issue**

- In the field we discovered that users would often go to a building, then speak to the owner first to **ask for permission** to collect data.
- As the building validation questions come first, they would resort to noting down the owners answers on another app, before going back to ODK Collect!
- The question order should be rethought to be most intuitive for the user.

**Proposed solution**

- The validation / digitization_correct was placed at the top so the fields could easily be hidden, to allow the user to edit below.
- This should be moved below the questions instead.
- They should still be hidden.

**Additional context**

- How do we best prevent the user overwriting the validation fields?
- We need the validation section to carry out conflation.
- The building selection will be handled by the custom ODK Collect version / load by intent feature, so this isn't an issue.

@ramyaragupathy as discussed

## Describe this PR
This PR contains works to test create project workflow.

## Screenshots
[Screencast from 24-7-24 01:18:24 अपराह्न +0545.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ceb219c2-0a57-4c6f-bb01-fbc934775123)

## Comment

From @spwoodcock: added multiple variants of running the tests:


```json
    "test:e2e": "CI=1 playwright test",
    "test:e2e-report": "playwright test",
    "test:e2e-debug": "playwright test --debug",
    "test:e2e-interactive": "playwright open http://fmtm.dev.test",
```

- `test:e2e` is the standard test that runs until completion, without starting the report UI.
- `test:e2e-report` starts the report UI afterwards to see the test output and traces.
- `test:e2e-debug` runs the browser in `--headful` mode (i.e. with a browser), allowing us to step through the test and see what it actually does in the UI.
- `test:e2e-interactive` also starts a web browser, but this time with a recording option, allowing us to write tests by recording the clicks we make on the UI.

All test also produce a trace.zip, which is a very helpful functionality to debug why a test may have failed:
- Go to a failed workflow: https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/actions/runs/10198097237
- Download the artifact `playwright-report.zip`.
- Open the index.html file to view the report.
- Extract the `.zip` file under `data` to get the traces.
- Go to `https://trace.playwright.dev` and uploaded the extracted traces.
- Step through the tests, with screenshots of the UI at a given point, plus logs of the network tab and console logs!

title: Injecting mandatory FMTM fields into custom XLSForms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Currently our XLSForm has hidden fields that are mandatory: feature / task selection, digitization_correct questions.
- This is prone to breakage if the user uploads a custom XLSForm and accidentally deletes fields (despite being hidden).
- We need a more resilient mechanism to allow for custom XLSForm upload flexbility, but also impose our restrictions / requirements that FMTM needs to function well.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Option 1: append the fields in the XLSForm, either via pyxlsx or possibly via Pandas, **prior to XLS --> XML**.
  - Load the XLSForm as a dataframe.
  - Have pre-prepared separate XLSForms with building questions & digitization_correct questions.
  - Read the building selection questions into a dataframe and append to start.
  - Read the digitization_correct questions into a dataframe and append to end.
  - However, this will introduce a big dependency: Pandas, which is not ideal.

- Option 2: use the current XML parsing / manipulation method to inject all required params, **after XLS --> XML**.
  - This method is possible, but may have many fields we need to insert into specific places.
  - Needs testing and is more prone to breakage.

**Additional context**

- This first option would probably require we update all form handling to use Pandas, which would be quite an improvement to XLS wrangling.

> [!Note]
> See comment below. We should not use Pandas, but instead `python-calamine`.

- As we use the Entity info for some stats like: number of features to map, number of submissions made, etc, we need to add a new Entity ideally.
- It should be added on form submission in ODK Collect using the `create_if` field with logic linked to the geopoint field.
- The status will be submitted as `2` MAPPED, so it should appear green on the map.

**Additional context**

After doing this we need to check:
- It doesn't break map rendering on ODK Collect map widget, if the user loads in Entities including a geopoint.
- The geopoint is displayed in OpenLayers on the project detail page of FMTM.

title: Project creation workflow 1: Basic
body:
## Problem

As part of the process of overhauling the project creation we have two flows:
- Basic with many defaults / pre-defined things.
- Advanced with a lot more configuration options.
- They should use the same project creation components, but just have a flag to `advanced=true`.

## Solution

- The first step to this is a splash page on project creation.
- The user selects: Basic or Advanced mapper flow, with a brief description for each.
- Clicking 'Basic' takes us to this flow

### 1. Project details

- Possibly simplify this down a bit.
- Combine the short and long description into one (ignore one of the fields).
- Do not add configuration for TMS URL here (can be added later if needed).
- Possibly remove the instructions field?

### 2. AOI

- Remains the same.
- Identify geometry type & ask if user wishes to merge multigeoms.

### 3. Category

- Only allow selection of category.
- No custom XLSForm upload?

### 4. Map Features

- Only allow for import from OSM, based on the category.
  - If the category if of type linestring, do not clip the extract from raw-data-api.
  - If the category is of type polygon/point, clip the extract from raw-data-api.
    
    This should avoid issues like below:
    ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18b3ea49-c6c8-4047-8128-c829458bedb4)

- Display the feature count to the user:
  - Possibly add a warning if a huge amount of features present >5000 ?
  - Useful for the user to know if their project is appropriately sized.

### 5. Splitting

- Keep the same.
- The data extract for splitting is automatically downloaded (as we selected OSM data extract).

**This issue is not final and should be updated**
Ref: https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/discussions/1328

title: Project creation workflow 1: Advanced
body:
## Problem

As part of the process of overhauling the project creation we have two flows:
- Basic with many defaults / pre-defined things.
- Advanced with a lot more configuration options.
- They should use the same project creation components, but just have a flag to `advanced=true`.

## Solution

- The first step to this is a splash page on project creation.
- The user selects: Basic or Advanced mapper flow, with a brief description for each.
- Clicking 'Advanced' takes us to this flow

### 1. Project details

- Keep all current options.

### 2. AOI

### 3. Category

- Allow for selection of category and bundled XLSForm is desired.
- Most likely the user will upload custom XLSForm, made easier by https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/1722

### 4. Map Features

title: Exceptions should use logger.exception, not logger.error
body:
**Describe the bug**

- We use `log.error` in most places, even when exceptions are raised.
- This is fine when viewing logs in the terminal.
- However to send via OTEL to tools like Sentry, the traceback is only included if `log.exception` is used.
  - This is essentially the same as `log.error(exc_info=True)`.
- If we want the full traceback stack to be included, then we need `log.exception("some info", stack_info=True)`

title: Document the process of using OData endpoints for data visualisation
body:
## Problem

Follow on from #1440

- FMTM facilitates data collection.
- OData endpoints are a standardised way to ingest this data into other tools: PowerBI, Tableau, Redash, Grafana
- ODK already has good docs on this that we should link to: https://docs.getodk.org/tutorial-mapping-households/

## Possible Solutions

- We probably need some extra docs to help flesh out how this can be achieved (based on actual requirements from a mapping project):
  - Submission history for each enumerator
  - Custom date range filtering of submissions
  - Total submissions vs total number features surveyed
  - Filter submissions by tasks
  - Average submission time per enumerator
  - Expected number of submissions vs actual daily submissions
  - Leaderboard based on submission
- Yes, PowerBI is proprietary, but it's free to use, very powerful, and user friendly. We need to be realistic and suggest the easiest solution that most end users will connect with. I would propose we document the process for PowerBI first.

### Additional Research

(from previous thread)

Describing various options in different forms.

#### Desktop Apps

- PowerBI is the simplest and most powerful. The files can be shared with other users of PowerBI Desktop. The dashboards cannot easily be shared on web however.
- Excel can also load OData, but it's not as visually appealing or easy to use as PowerBI.
- Haven't tested Tableau, but it's meant to be good (less powerful that PowerBI).

#### Hosted Solutions

Note with these options we need to pay to host them...

- ~Redash, acquired by databricks… (limping on as OSS currently, so let's see where it goes)~
- ~Apache Superset & Metabase don’t support OData~
- Grafana has an OData plugin and is a fantastic CNCF project.
  - Probably our best choice until we discover something else.
  - A bit of a pain to configure the data provider / dashboard, but works.
  - https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/dvelop-odata-datasource/
  - Docker compose config to test it:
    ```yaml
    services:
      grafana:
        image: grafana/grafana-oss:11.2.0
        container_name: grafana
        restart: unless-stopped
        ports:
         - '3022:3000'
        environment:
          GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS: dvelop-odata-datasource
        volumes:
          - grafana-storage:/var/lib/grafana
    
    volumes:
      grafana-storage:
    ```

#### Web

- We could possibly use the XOData chrome extension, but it looks a bit old. Not tested.
- Final option is to make our own simple dashboard using a Graph library (charts.js or Apache ECharts) and HTML tables.
  - The creds for OData endpoints would need either be:
    - Embedded in the web app - not an option 😅 
    - Configured by the user - not that user friendly.

## Summary

In summary this is a tough decision!

**Recommendation**:

- Have simple visualisations for most common requirements built into FMTM (as we do currently, but improved upon).
- For more complex / bespoke needs, just ask the user to install PowerBI and make a dashboard (this could be done for them by sharing a pre-configured `.pbix` file dashboard).

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Users can be frustrated they can't see the task areas in ODK Collect too.

- This would allow users to see the FMTM task areas alongside the features to map.

To achieve this we would need to bundle a tool like tippecanoe, then run:

```bash
tippecanoe --output=task_polygons_119.mbtiles task_polygons_119.geojson
```

**Additional context**

1. This is very low priority, as if we have loading by intent full integrated (feature pre-selection), this isn't really that necessary.
2. Ideally we can do this without tippecanoe, as it's a very simple process. An entirely JS implementation would be ideal...

title: Minor frontend updates for better wording / explanations in project creation
body:
Based on discussions with @ramyaragupathy and user feedback.

## Issue

- Select 'Category' is no longer good terminology, as we basically use custom XLSForms for all projects now.

- The secondary dataset upload functionality is not explained.

- Info about coordinate systems is not clear on geojson upload. While ideally the use should know about coordinate systems if creating a project, this may not always be the case. GeoJSON is a tricky dataset in that it rarely includes the coordinate system. Normally they should be EPSG4326, but they could equally be web mercator, or even another coordinate system entirely 😅 

## Solution

- Rename 'Select Category' --> 'Upload Survey'
- Add a small bit of info explaining why uploading a secondary geojson might be useful - for mapping features that have related features (e.g. buildings, selecting the road it falls on).
- Inform the user that geojson uploads should be in EPSG 4326 coordinate system.

title: Make submission data downloads only possible for project contributors
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Currently anyone can download data for a public project.
- It might not be very clear to the project manager / users that this is the case.
- Sometimes sensitive data is collected.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Limit download of submissions to either:
  - Org manager, project manager.
  - Contributors (i.e. contributing mappers or validators).

**Other considerations**

Do we need an extra flag for projects `sensitive` that applies a submission view / downloading restriction to project admins and above?

There were issues with custom additional entities `geojson` properties which weren't supported by odk-central failing the creation of entities and dataset properties. Some keywords of `odk-central` such as `uuid`, name, label are not supported by `odk-central` to avoid duplicate entries.

title: Replace `pdm` dependency solver with `uv`
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [ ] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [x] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Describe this PR

uv:
- `uv` was released not too long ago and has since almost gained feature parity with other tools like `pdm`.
- It's written in `rust` and is orders of magnitude faster at locking dependencies: a minor win, but a nice one nonetheless.
- It also allows you to run different versions of Python on your system very easily.
- Thanks @Pradip-p for pointing this tool out!

What I did:
- Replaced all usage of `pdm` with `uv`.
- Overhauled the backend dockerfile to work with `uv` and be a bit cleaner.
- Updated docs around using `pdm`.

Minor caveats:
- We can no longer use the `dynamic` field in `pyproject.toml`: `dynamic=["version"]`.
- This isn't a big deal - we can just hardcode it. The version updating is done by `commitizen` anyway, so nothing lost.

Bonus:
- There is also a pre-commit hook for `uv`, allowing us to re-lock automatically if someone updates the a backend dependency and forgets to lock 🎉 (which would break the docker build otherwise).

Key things of note:
- `uv lock` re-locks dependencies, including all optional groups.
- `uv sync` installs dependencies locally.
- `uv run ...` runs a command using installed dependencies venv.
- It's also possible to manage multiple python versions on the system with `uv python list` and `uv python install`.
- `pdm publish` --> `uv publish` for publishing to pypi.

Note: I plan to talk about using this tool with the dev teams when I visit NAXA 👍 

## Screenshots

A fresh lock takes 1 second:

title: Remove trailing slashes from endpoints, fix check_access for backend roles
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [ ] 🍕 Feature
- [x] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [x] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [ ] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Describe this PR

Trailing slashes, Origin header, and CORS:
- I removed all trailing slashes from routes in FastAPI.
- Proper REST APIs should distinguish between `/route/` and `/route` - they are different.
- We were getting an automatic 307 redirect from FastAPI from `/route` --> `/route/`, which was causing the `Origin` request header to be stripped in Firefox. As a result, with `Origin: null` the CORS check could not complete, so we get a CORS error.
- I removed this default functionality from FastAPI.
- In future all APIs should not end in a trailing slash. Frontend calls should also account for this.

Fixes check_access logic:
- The logic for check_access on the roles was broken a bit.
- If no org_id was passed, then we need to extract the org_id from the project - fixed this.
- I also updated the `project_roles` dict to correctly return when user details are returned from the APIs.
- Finally, I converted the project role enum values into numerical values for assessing the hierarchy in check_access.

title: Backend: OSM login enforced for management, additional temp login option for mappers
body:
**Describe the bug**

- Follow up to #1890
- We have removed the temp login button from the management frontend.
The mapper frontend accepts both OSM and temp login options.
- The backend API remains the same though. 
- A user that logs in using 'temp token' in the mapper frontend, but then goes to the management frontend, will still show as logged in.

**Solutions**

- This isn't so simple as it first seems.
- We use separate cookies for each login type which is good.
- But as we use the same API for both frontends, how do we determine from which frontend the user makes the call from?
- The only approach I can think of for now is to gave seaprate endpoints:
  - We call different refresh endpoints, like `refresh_management` and `refresh_mapper` from each frontend. 
  - This would mean we can ignore the `_temp` cookie for the management frontend.

Of course, also open to other ideas!

title: Tokha discussion additonal requirements
body:
## 4 Requirements

### High Priority

#### Multiple Feature Selection At Once

- Ability to select two geometries as part of a form.
- This requires creating a second entity list (done).
- One option is via ODK (the current setup):
  - Extra question injected into XLSForm.
  - User selects one geometry in one question.
  - Selects associated geometry in another question.
- However, a more ideal scenario would be to solve this via the FMTM map UI:
  - User selects one geometry.
  - Popup appears to 'Map Feature', with an extra button to 'select associated geometry'.
  - User selects second geom.
  - User clicks button to 'Map Feature'.
  - ODK form is opened with both geometries pre-selected (via URL params).
  - To facilitate this perhaps we need a flag / db record that the user opted for multiple geometries?
	
#### Adding New Geometries Via FMTM

- We added a geopoint capability.
- This needs to be more advanced.
- We need building polygon and road polyline addition too.
- Probably possible in ODK via form.
- Ideally also solved via FMTM mapping library.
  - Create new geom, then open in ODK.
  - Send the new geometry as javarosa string to to the form as intent field.

### Low Priority

#### Submission Download Filtering

- Filtering by date is useful.
- Particularly in workflow that require validation on a daily basis (as new data comes in).

#### Displaying Recently Digitised Buildings

- Show recently digitised buildings to the enumerator.
- In ODK:
  - We could achieve this by updating the `create_if` logic for the entity and adding the new geom to the entities list.
  - It would display the next time the user views the geometries in a question.
- In FMTM:
  - This is harder as we rely on the flatgeobuf geometry!
  - Needs more thought it going this route.

title: Project stats choropleth range is based on total submissions for project, not per task
body:
**Describe the bug**

Here we have all task areas, either blue or red:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cba332b5-0f17-491b-906d-ae2cab55e25b)

The range of the choropleth think is based on the total submissions for the project.
Instead it should be based on the maximum number of submissions for a task area.

pseudocode
```
task_area_submissions = get_number_of_submissions_per_task()
Min: 0
Max: max(task_area_submissions)
```

The max would be a much lower number and show the range of colours correctly.

title: Clean polygon geometries; remove holes, fix right hand rule
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [X] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [X] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [ ] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Related Issue

- Issue:  #1904 

## Describe this PR

This PR updates the postgis utils to clean the polygon geojson before any operations such as split by square , split by algorithm, create project outline, generate data extracts. It includes:

- `remove_holes`: It checks for any holes present in the polygon and removes it using exterior ring
- `ensure_right_hand_rule`: It ensures each polygon follows right hand rule
- `create_single_polygon`: It creates a single polygon, mostly a project outline case, while creating projects or generating data extracts. Here, if the geojson has disjoint multipolygons, then it applies a convex hull to create a single AOI, or else it will use an exterior ring to create a single AOI. During data extracts, it won't apply convex hull; we will get data extracts in individual polygons inside MulitPolygon.

With exterior ring for normal multipolygon case:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99f57585-b5d0-49dd-8efd-5ed06cab9be9)

With disjoint mulitpolygon:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ca6de70-190b-44ef-bc0c-62312f598b71)

Single AOI for both cases:
Case I: After removing holes, fixing right hand rule and merging all polygons
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6a31ad7-d751-422a-b14b-602f7c7d1e5a)

Case II: Disjoint Multipolygon creating single AOI

## Related Issue

Related to https://github.com/hotosm/fmtm/issues/1915

## Describe this PR

- Our current workflow to draw new geoms in ODK is fine.
- But in order to open up options in the future, I added `terradraw` to allow creating the point geom in the FMTM map, then open ODK Collect with the `new_feature` field already filled out.
- The advantage is that the mapper can see all existing geoms while they draw a new one, including additional geometries that we can load on the map to help facilitate the placement.

- Please check over all of my logic & test this thoroughly @Sujanadh @Anuj-Gupta4 @NSUWAL123 @manjitapandey

- I removed the 'Temporary Login' card / option from the mapper frontend.

title: Addition of distance constraints between user's geolocation and feature selected for mapping
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, user can select the feature far away from their current location. This causes enumerators to share incorrect data sometimes. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Restrict the user to select the feature that are far away from their current location. For that we need to necessarily ask for geolocation on mapper's page and if users click on feature far away and click on map on odk. The error message saying the feature you are trying to map is xx km away from your current location.

title: Create new DB table to store 'new' and 'bad' geoms
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- When a new geometry is mapped (submission made), its not displayed on the map.
- When a geom is marked bad, its hidden within the task. You have to click the task to see bad geom.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Database table recording new and bad geoms.
- Synced to user via electric.
- Bad geoms displayed flashing on top of the map.
- New geoms displayed either on top, or when you click a task area only?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Ideally we could add new geoms to the entity list. Does this work currently?
- Will there be issues if its a different geometry type to the other geoms (collecting a point in a building entity list)?
- However this would mean the user has to refresh the page to view new geoms, plus we don't have a nice way to do this currently anyway. Loading geoms is based on the flatgeobuf, then entity properties are mapped to the geometries by id.
- Using a new db table opens the possibility for real time sync of new geoms.

title: Warn user if they create a new geometry that is far from their geolocation
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- If the user clicks to create a new map feature, but the point is very far from their location, we should warn them.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Currently when the user clicks for the point, it redirects to ODK Collect immediately.
- We should add a check before that:
  - `if geolocation is enabled` && `if clicked point is more than 50m from current location`, do not redirect.
  - Instead open a confirmation dialog / modal: 'The created geometry is far away from your current location. Are you sure you wish to proceed?'
  - If the user clicks 'Yes', then continue with the ODK Collect redirect / intent, if 'No', then remove the point from the map (but keep drawing enabled!)

title: Provide organisational admins with ODK credentials if needed
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Followed by [discussion on slack](https://hotosm.slack.com/archives/C04PCBFDEGN/p1736079538785119), Any organisation admins should be able to choose HOTOSM as an organisation to create a project. 

**Why would people do that**
Sometimes an organisation may not have their own odk central server for storing submissions. In those cases, they can create an organisation but can choose HOTOSM as an organisation during project creation so that submission would be stored on HOTOSM odk server.  Although, they should be admin of any organisation to be able to do so since only organisation admins should be able to create projects. 

We may have further discussion in long term regarding this. May be they can still use their organisation details but use HOT's odk central.

title: As a user, it's not clear to me that I need to log into the mapper frontend
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- When I load the mapper frontend, by default I am logged in as 'localadmin'.
- This is an implementation detail that as a user I don't care about.
- To log in I have to 'log out', then log in again as my user.
- I am not informed that this is necessary for my edits to be attributed.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Hide 'localadmin':
- If the user is 'localadmin', i.e. the temp auth is used, then this should be hidden from the user.
- Instead, from the user perspective, the UI should be shown as logged out (the Sign In option should be present).
- When the user signs in, the token generated will override the temp auth token, and the user details will be shown at the top right.

Inform the user they should log in:
- We need a way to inform the user that they need to log in to be attributed with their edits.
- Instead, perhaps at the top right, instead of 'localadmin', we show 'Not logged in'.
- A tooltip could be shown when hovering that text to say 'You must log in for your edits to be attributed to your user account.'

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- This could be done via the project setup promps, but would probably become too cluttered.

title: Add API keys functionality to assist external integrations
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Currently there is no easy way for external services to GET or POST data to FMTM.
- A typical way to do this would be API keys, with restricted API access / functionality.
- The keys should be scoped to specific actions / endpoints, with minimal attack surface if misused (stored insecurely) and compromised.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- [ ] Add an `api_key` field to the user table, default empty.
- [ ] If the user requests a token, then generate one in the db.
- [ ] An API guard dependency to check for valid api key before proceeding.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- An oauth based flow for this, but it would be significantly more complex for little gain.

**Additional context**

- We should only expose a small amount of endpoints that accept API keys.
- This is to minimise the attach surface if an API key is compromised by a user and misused by malicious actors.

title: Notify existing FMTM users if public project is created within their city or some proximity radius
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Most FMTM users who log in to FMTM aren't sure which project to choose for mapping since they have to be near project location for mapping. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Encourage users to add their approximate location (choose location on map) or city from their user's settings page. This location should be editable so that if user migrate to other location, they can still be able to change their location for field mapping. And when the project is created, we can tally the location of existing users and notify them so that local people are aware of projects nearby for mapping. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

**Additional context**
Any suggestions are welcomed. Its just a raw idea.

title: Further develop / refine the splitter workflow to specify a number of enumerators
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Current workflow is based of average number of buildings required.
- Sometimes the team has a number of enumerators / mappers, and would like a number of tasks to match that.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- We should have a separate workflow, that is wrapped in the same `split_by_sql` function but with a different param.
- The param should be `num_of_enumerators`.
- If specified, the SQL will ensure we get exactly that number of tasks, then split up the tasks based on an approximate even distribution of features, also factoring the roads/rivers as usual.

**Additional context**

- To facilitate this we probably need modular functions.
- We should have some common logic defined in one place, that is reused across multiple workflows:
  - num buildings
  - num enumerators

title: Add a splitting workflow that accounts for terrain
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- We account for OSM features, and other params such as average number of buildings per task.
- It would be great if we could also account for terrain!
  - So we don't request users walk off a cliff!
  - So users can avoid having to go up and down hills and can map features roughly at the same altitude.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Add an extra part of the modular workflow to account for terrain, if available.
- Graceful fallback if no terrain data available?

title: Add login to frontend via unified HOT login
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

For context on the FieldTM redesign:
1. First I wanted to not save the created projects at all, instead being a simple frontend that creates projects in the downstream tool. I think based on feedback and reflecting, I decided to save the projects to a small db, so people at least have a rough idea of ongoing projects in FieldTM (tracking purposes mostly...)
2. Second I also didn't want to include any login requirement, relying on credentials being provisioned in the downstream app and then input into FieldTM. To make the experience a bit easier for users, I since decided we will continue to bundle ODK Central + QFieldCloud as part of the install, meaning that people will create projects in our hosted tools & need a login of sorts.

So login for FieldTM is a bit unique:
- Login for managers is mostly just a formality for (1) tracking who creates projects (2) provide a small barrier for bots creating projects
- Once a project is created, there isn't much need for FieldTM, so managers have credentials in the downstream app (not managed with HOT login)
- Mappers don't use HOT login either, as they log directly into the mobile apps: ODK Collect or QField
- We could possibly add HOT login as an OpenID Connect provider to QField + QFieldCloud, a feature proposed and supposedly being worked on by the Hanko team: https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/discussions/860#discussioncomment-14883079 (so users can login using HOT login directly in their QField app). But let's not look at this for now.
- There is no longer a concept of private projects in FieldTM - privacy constraints are set downstream via e.g. QField, if they are needed.

❗ I would propose we only add HOT login to the main website, required to create projects.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Integrate HOT login as the primary login approach (it include OSM + others underneath).
- Once logged in, users can access the project creation page.
- We should consider how this integrates with API keys! As FieldTM also has login capability using an Authorization header of `X-API-Token`. It guess there should be no conflict, but please consider this in whatever is implemented.
- No login is required to access the project summary and project details page though.

title: The ODK form currently has no task locking capabilities
body:
## Issue

- The user selects a task area, which filters down the features.
- The features change colour based on mapping status / complete or not.
- However there is no way to mark a task area as 'locked for mapping'.

## Solutions

- First off, do we even need this? Let's see based on user feedback if task locking is required.
- That said, task assignment is definitely a valuable thing (based on previous feedback). Perhaps we can have a task assignment form for ODK, where a manager/user will choose a task area and enter an OSM username to assign?

### 1. Typical 'lock task' --> 'map feature' workflow, using two forms

- Form A - lock task areas:
  - survey.save_to for task `status` entity property.
  - Can we use conditional logic for the `fill` entity property somehow, or do we also need to `save_to` for this?
  - The user returns to this form to map is as 'fully mapped' when complete, so we can change the colour to indicate it's complete to other mappers.
- Form B - map features
  - First filter task entities with choice_filter status = 'locked'.
  - Then select from features entities via choice_filter for only the selected task area (the user has to select the task area twice in a row, in two separate forms...).
  - Use a `save_to` to set the status field of the feature to mapped.

### 2. Simple task assignment approach, using two forms

- In this scenario, typically task areas don't need to be locked to be mapped.
- Instead, we can have a form that is used for 'task assignment'.
- If a manager or user wishes to assign a task to a specific user, they can click the task area and enter their OSM username.
- The task area colour can be changed to indicate it's "assigned".
- When the mapper it's assigned to open the mapping form, we could also filter down the task areas to their assigned tasks (if desirable).

### 3. Post-processing / webhook approach

- Instead of managing task areas via forms, we could do it on submission.
- Using `central-webhook`, we could execute a service that determines:
  - If a task area has any mapped features, then lock the task.
  - If all the features are mapped in the task, then mark as complete.
  - If any features are marked "bad", then also mark the task as with issues to address.
- This is a more complex setup, but is probably the best user experience out of all the approaches.

**Note**

- For QField, we plan to solve this a different way, using a plugin for task locking and assignment (small QField UI buttons).

title: GNSS spoofing possible mitigations
body:
This is an aggregation of info from multiple source, done by Codex 5.4.

## Problem

* It’s becoming increasingly common to see large-scale GNSS/GPS spoofing in the wild, e.g. suspected state-level interference during regional conflicts (such as activity attributed to Iran in recent reporting in the middle east).
* GNSS denial (jamming) is also widely deployed, for example in urban environments to prevent drone operations (e.g. reported cases in Medellín).
* These attacks impact:

  * UAV/drone navigation
  * Mapping and surveying workflows
  * Mobile/location-based applications
  * Safety-critical systems relying on positioning

A key constraint: **civilian GNSS (e.g. GPS) signals are not authenticated**, making spoofing fundamentally hard to prevent using commodity hardware.

---

## Detection

Detection is currently the most accessible capability on consumer devices.

### On smartphones

- Install GNSS Logger 
- There is a Spoof/Jam tab on the app.
- You can run the tests to see if jamming / spoofing is detected.

* Apps such as [GNSS Logger](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.location.gps.gnsslogger) (Google) can:

  * Expose raw GNSS measurements
  * Indicate potential jamming/spoofing conditions
* Typical indicators:

  * Sudden jumps in position
  * Inconsistent satellite constellations
  * Signal-to-noise anomalies
  * Time inconsistencies

However:

* Phones lack reliable access to full navigation message data
* Detection is **heuristic, not cryptographically verifiable**
* No real mitigation - only awareness

### On dedicated receivers

Higher-end GNSS receivers allow:

* Monitoring of multiple constellations (GPS, Galileo, BeiDou)
* Multi-frequency comparison (e.g. L1 vs L5)
* Detection of signal anomalies

Still:

* Most systems detect spoofing but **cannot guarantee correctness**

---

## Possible Mitigations

There is no single solution - effective systems combine multiple layers.

### 1. Multi-band + multi-constellation GNSS

* Use receivers supporting:

  * Multiple frequencies (L1 + L5)
  * Multiple constellations (GPS, Galileo, BeiDou)
* Benefit:

  * Spoofing all signals simultaneously is significantly harder

---

### 2. External GNSS receivers (vs phone-only)

* Consumer phones are insufficient for robust positioning under attack
* Use external receivers with:

  * Raw measurement access
  * Stable antennas
* Feed processed results to mobile devices (Bluetooth/WiFi)

---

### 3. Sensor fusion (GNSS + IMU)

* Combine GNSS with:

  * Accelerometers
  * Gyroscopes
* Detect:

  * Physically impossible motion
  * Divergence between inertial and GNSS position

Limitation:

* Drift accumulates without GNSS correction

---

### 4. Alternative positioning approaches

* Visual localization (requires pre-built 3D maps)
* Dead reckoning
* Infrastructure-based positioning

These are:

* Environment-specific
* Not universally deployable - require small 3D models

---

### 5. Networked / shared positioning

Proposed architecture:

* A **trusted GNSS node**:

  * High-quality receiver
  * Spoofing detection + validation
* Broadcast to nearby users via Bluetooth/WiFi:

```json
{
  "position": "...",
  "confidence": "HIGH | SUSPECT",
  "authenticated": true,
  "anomaly_score": 0.1
}
```

Benefit:

* Reduces reliance on each device independently trusting GNSS

### 6. Other resources / options

There is some good info out there - mostly requiring specialist equipment:

- Mitigation techniques summary 2024:
https://gpspatron.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Selecting-Optimal-Anti-Spoofing-and-Anti-Jamming-Techniques-for-Resilient-GNSS.pdf

Old info about detection on arrival signal correction (possible mitigation, but needs equipment / is complex:
https://insidegnss.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/mayjune17-WP.pdf

---

## Implementing Encrypted GNSS

One of the most promising civilian approaches is authentication via Galileo OSNMA.

### What OSNMA provides

* Cryptographic signing of navigation messages
* Verification using:

  * ECDSA public keys
  * TESLA key chains
* Allows receivers to confirm:

  * Navigation data is authentic
  * Data has not been modified

This directly addresses **spoofed navigation messages**.

---

### Using `galileo-osnma`

The [galileo-osnma](https://github.com/daniestevez/galileo-osnma) project:

* Rust implementation of OSNMA
* Works in embedded environments (low memory footprint)
* Can validate Galileo navigation data in real time

This makes it suitable for:

* Custom GNSS receivers
* Embedded systems
* UAV/navigation stacks

---

### Practical architecture

A viable implementation:

1. **Hardware**

   * Multi-band GNSS receiver (e.g. u-blox ZED-F9P class)
   * External antenna

> [!NOTE]
> u-blox EVK-F9P-01 GNSS dev kit is approx 300 USD.
> It receives RAWX (raw GNSS) and NAV messages (for OSNMA), works with Raspberry Pis, uses embedded Linux, has a huge ecosystem (ArduPilot support etc).

2. **Processing layer**

   * Embedded device (e.g. Raspberry Pi)
   * Run:

     * GNSS parsing
     * `galileo-osnma` verification
     * Signal anomaly checks

3. **Distribution**

   * Broadcast validated position via:

     * Bluetooth
     * WiFi / mesh

4. **Clients (phones, drones, apps)**

   * Consume:

     * Position
     * Authentication status
     * Confidence metrics

---

### Key limitations

* OSNMA is still rolling out across the Galileo constellation
* Not supported/exposed on most smartphones
* Does **not fully prevent**:

  * Replay attacks (meaconing)
  * Signal overpowering

### Alternative projects

- Python implementation: https://github.com/Algafix/OSNMA
- ESA is apparently developing "Signal Authentication Service (SAS): will enable an authenticated positioning free-of-charge service by complementing the OSNMA with E6-based ranging authentication capabilities targeting to support civil applications." (source https://www.gsc-europa.eu/galileo/services). This will likely be a HTTP API or something that can be integrated into apps?)

---

### Bottom line

* Consumer devices alone cannot reliably mitigate GNSS spoofing
* Detection is possible, mitigation requires **dedicated hardware + layered approach**
* OSNMA is a critical building block, but must be combined with:

  * Multi-band receivers
  * Sensor fusion
  * System-level validation

A practical path forward is to build a **shared, trusted GNSS node** using external hardware and OSNMA verification, and distribute validated positioning data to end-user devices.

title: We need a task assignment UI
body:
- It's clear from field testing that most field campaigns actually operate on a 'assign in advance' basis, rather than an 'assign in the field' approach.
- We need a UI to display task areas on a map.
- The task can be assigned to specific users / groups via comment.
- Task can be grouped for assignment in bulk to a group (i.e. higher level task division, say 4 groups, one NE one SW one SE one NW section, with many assigned tasks within each quadrant).
- The UI would load the tasks geojson from the fieldtm db, then all edits would be made in-browser (localstorage perhaps?). Once complete, the user 'confirms' the assignments, then this will pull the qfieldcloud geopackage, add task assignment fields, then push back to qfieldcloud. For ODK this would be updating the entity properties for the task.
- This approach also facilitates field mapping via tools like CoMaps / Organic Maps, as we can do the assignment - similar to field papers, but tasks that are more field-appropriate - then send the tasks into the app alongside the data.

title: feat: task assignment UI for project managers (#3095)
body:
## What

A first, **"assign in advance"** task assignment UI for project managers, addressing #3095. Managers get a panel on the project details page that shows task areas on a map, lets them select tasks and apply an assignee + group label (with one-click quadrant auto-grouping for the NE/SW/SE/NW bulk case), and persists assignments as feature properties on the existing `task_areas_geojson`.

This is opened as a **draft for discussion** — it implements the durable "edit in the browser, confirm to save" half of the issue. The field-device sync (QFieldCloud geopackage / ODK entity push) and the CoMaps `.kmz` export (#3064) are deliberately deferred to follow-up PRs (see _Deferred_ below). I'd value a steer on the open questions before going further.

## How it fits the existing architecture

No SPA, no build step, no new dependencies, no schema change — entirely server-rendered LiteStar + HTMX + Jinja2 with a flat static JS file, per `AGENTS.md` and the existing decisions.

Two commits:

1. **`fix(backend): stabilize task_id across save and export paths`** — a small prerequisite refactor. Task ids were assigned positionally and divergently in the QField (`_build_tasks_geojson`) and ODK (`_build_task_entities`) export paths, so the two ecosystems could disagree on task identity. This stamps a persistent, collision-safe integer `task_id` into `task_areas_geojson` features on save and makes both export builders read the stored id. This is the keystone the assignment feature keys on, and is independently useful — happy to split it into its own PR if you'd prefer.

2. **`feat(htmx): task assignment map panel for project managers`** — the panel itself:
   - New `app/htmx/assignment/` module with three `project_manager`-gated routes: a lazy-loaded panel fragment, a JSON `assignments/geojson` endpoint (tasks merged with `assigned_to` / `assigned_group`), and a `POST` save.
   - `save_task_assignments` service alongside `save_task_areas`: validates the group label (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$`), caps/sanitises the assignee, rejects unknown task ids, merges into feature properties under a `FOR UPDATE` row lock, and **never writes `status`** — task state stays owned by the field apps.
   - `task_assignment.js` (flat file, reuses the global Leaflet): click / shift-click selection shared between map and table, quadrant auto-grouping, draft edits staged in `sessionStorage` (matching the existing `ftm-draft-aoi-outline` precedent) and replayed over fresh server data, all user values rendered via `textContent` only.
   - Confirm warnings on the data-extract / re-split steps when stored assignments would be discarded.

## Screenshots

**Assignment panel** — task areas on a map, quadrant-coloured by group, with the summary table below:

![Assignment panel](https://github.com/kartikey54/field-tm/releases/download/fieldtm-3095-assets/01-assignment-panel.png)

**Selecting tasks** — click / shift-click on the map and table, then apply an assignee + group to the selection:

![Selecting tasks](https://github.com/kartikey54/field-tm/releases/download/fieldtm-3095-assets/02-selection.png)

**After saving** — assignments persisted to feature properties and reflected in the table:

![After saving](https://github.com/kartikey54/field-tm/releases/download/fieldtm-3095-assets/03-saved-table.png)

## Tests

34 new tests (`tests/htmx/test_assignment_routes.py`, plus task-id stability coverage in `test_finalize_odk.py` / `test_qfield_routes.py`): route registration and auth, geojson shape and defaults, the save happy path (incl. `HX-Trigger` payload and that `status` is never written), XSS escaping, validation rejects (bad group label, overlong assignee, unknown task id, missing payload), the empty/`{}` no-split sentinel, and cross-builder task-id agreement. Local backend suite: **305 passed, 0 failed** (the two ODK-Central / QGIS-container suites were not run locally).

## Deliberately deferred (happy to sequence as follow-ups)

- **ODK entity sync** — push `assigned_to` / `assigned_group` to the `tasks` dataset entities (most machinery already exists in `central_crud`).
- **QFieldCloud sync** — pull `tasks.gpkg`, merge assignment fields by `task_id`, push back; plus stopping `_add_plugin_task_fields` from clobbering assignments on regeneration.
- **CoMaps / Organic Maps `.kmz` export** (#3064).
- **Field status read-back** (showing live task progress on the manager's map) — depends on the sync work above.

## Open questions

1. **Storage shape:** assignments as `task_areas_geojson` feature properties (this PR) vs a relational `task_assignments` table (audit trail, row-level locking). I went properties-first to keep this PR schema-free; would you want the table from the start?
2. **Permissions:** nothing in the codebase appears to write `user_roles`, so `project_manager` only resolves for global admins in deployments today. Should project creators get a project-admin role at creation?
3. **Assignee identity:** free-text `assigned_to` (covers account-less mappers / shared QFC accounts) with opportunistic QFC-collaborator suggestions — acceptable, or should assignment drive per-mapper QFC user provisioning?
4. **Groups:** is the free-text `assigned_group` label the right model for the quadrant use case, or did you envision groups of *users*?
5. **Single-task projects** (`task_areas_geojson == {}`): this PR shows a "split first" callout rather than materialising a synthetic single task — OK?

---

Refs #3095. Related #3064.

title: Reliable submission sync for ODK field mappers with intermittent connectivity
body:
Hi,

I've been following Field-TM and I wanted to raise a sync reliability question that ZamSync was built to address.

When a field mapper works in an area with intermittent connectivity, ODK Collect queues submissions locally. If the connection drops after the server receives a submission but before it sends an acknowledgment, the mapper's device retries and Central gets a duplicate. If the connection drops before the server receives it, the submission is lost unless the mapper notices the error.

ZamSync approaches this differently: an append-only WAL on the device records every submission locally first, then syncs using Version Vectors to track exactly what each peer has seen. Reconnecting after hours offline sends only the delta, with deduplication built into the protocol. No double submissions, no loss on power cut.

It's a static Rust binary, under 10 MB RAM, so it fits on the low-spec Android devices common in field mapping contexts.

Concrete question: in Field-TM, when mappers go offline for extended periods and reconnect, what does the current failure mode look like? Does ODK Central coordinate with Field-TM to deduplicate submissions, or is that handled client-side by ODK Collect?

GitHub: https://github.com/Etoile-Bleu/ZamSync
Deep dive: https://dev.to/etoile_bleu/-i-built-a-sync-engine-for-clinics-that-run-on-2g-and-lose-power-mid-transfer-here-is-why-and-18od

title: REST API endpoints for integration with HOT Portal
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There's no way to get data about FieldTM projects in a programatic way other than scrapping the HTML.

For example, we would like to get "all user projects" from the HOT's Portal (once shared auth is implemented.

Also, we're already getting projects for adding them to a "Plan" in Portal, but because there's no API, we have to scrap the HTML, a non-ideal solution (there's no documentation, HTML can change, ...)

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A REST API would be ideal, because is what we're using on all other HOT Tools, but if not it could be also other like GraphQL or SOAP (please no 😁)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Scrapping the HTML, which is what we are already doing, but not ideal.

**Additional context**

We want to better integrate FieldTM with other tools, specially in the context of the Portal, which is the single point of access to all our tools and data, but also for other use cases like:

- Create a FieldTM-QField project with a selected OAM base layer
- Create a FieldTM-QField project with the result of a selected Drone Tasking Manager project
- Create a FieldTM project for the sam AOI defined for a Tasking Manager project

For starting, we need these endpoints:

* `/api/projects` - If the user is logged in, it should return all user projects. Minimum data for each one: title and id. App would be also useful (QField, ODK, ...) and centroid or image would help for better presentation.
* `/api/project/<project_id>` - Same info that in the list but for an individual project. It should work for both logged and un-logged users.

We can discuss other endpoints in the future once we would want to have more integration (like the examples that I mentioned above), but for now we are good with those.

Thanks!!

title: Shared HOT login
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We are implementing shared login (based on Hanko) on all HOT tools. The goal is to make tools more accessible, easier to use and have better coupling between them.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Implement shared login like we have in Drone Tasking Manager, ChatMap, HOT's uMap and Portal.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Not having login at all, but it will be difficult to integrate Field TM as part of a integral solution (the HOT Tech Suite)

**Additional context**

There's a branch already in place with a draft implementation, it must be updated to be ready for review.

title: Splitting algorithm: simply split by every road present in AOI
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Related to: https://github.com/hotosm/field-tm/issues/3018
- If the user is collecting street imagery, it makes sense to prioritise splitting along roads only (as they will walk / cycle roads to capture imagery)
- We could ideally have an algorithm that simply splits by all roads in the AOI.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Grab all the major and minor roads in OAM.
- Do a simple `ST_Polygonize` to generate polygons inside the intersecting areas of roads?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Areas could be simple buffered polygons around the road linestrings, split at intersections?
- Users would select a 'road' to map, instead of a polygon area, which might make more sense for projects like this?

title: Mapping app: add SketchMap
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- [SketchMapTool](https://sketch-map-tool.heigit.org) does a few things, but a key piece of functionality allows users to collect field data by drawing it, then scanning in the collected info and having it digitised automatically.
- SketchMap doesn't have built in coordination though.
- So FieldTM could be used to split an area into field mappable chunks, then via https://github.com/hotosm/field-tm/issues/3095 we could assign task areas to users.
- Users would visit their assigned task area, then proceed to collect data by drawing it on the pre-printed maps they have in the field.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- User creates a SketchMap project in FieldTM, including task splitting based on required params.
  - The 'Finalise' stage will need to call the SketchMap API to create a project.
  - The task assignment UI will probably also need to call the SketchMap API to assign usernames somewhere in SketchMap?
- The user scans a QRCode in FieldTM, which takes them to their assigned area in SketchMap tool.
- They then print out their maps for the field, then go to the field (or a project manager does this for them?)
- Data is collected by hand, then scanned into SketchMap.

**Additional Info**

Needs discussion with HeiGIT to propose exactly how this integration would work.

title: Updates to the QField-FieldTM plugin
body:
## Insights after testing

- A major flaw with the "task locking in the field" approach is that people don't know who locks what task areas immediately, so there is initial confusion.
- Having real-time task locking / UI updates would probably help, something we attempted with the 'mapper frontend' a few years ago, but it's not realistic to assume connectivity requirements for this. Plus we don't have that capability in ODK / QField / or other tools.
- Pre-assignment of tasks is more likely the way to go, using an assignment UI for preparation before going to the field.
- The FieldTM plugin for QField needs some tweaks to account for this.

## Grouping tasks

- It's very common for field mapping 'groups' to form. While it's possible to map as individuals, it's not as fun, safe, or rewarding. Groups could be only two people, or more.
- It seems logical to lump together tasks into another layer: **groups**.
- The FieldTM assignment UI works around groups:
  1. A number of groups are defined, e.g. by colour.
  2. Tasks are then grouped (e.g. by colour)
  3. Each mapping group then works in their coloured zone for the day.
  4. The subdivision of tasks within a group is done informally in the field: "me and Wilson will map tasks 2 and 3, if you and Chomba map tasks 4 and 6."
- This structure allows for some flexibility:
  - Example: a team of 5 mappers can all decide to map the 'blue' tasks for the day, subdividing tasks 1-10 amongst themselves.
  - Example: a team of 100 mappers can divide into 10 groups with team leads, with each team assigned a group colour. Within the teams / groups, then subdivide tasks amongst the mappers.

**All assignment is done in the Field-TM UI. This updates symbologies in QField and guides people through the mapping process. To update the assignment, the manager / team leads will return to the Field-TM UI to do further splitting**.

## The QField plugin

### Requirements for v1

1. Button to "join a group" (this then influences the labels / symbology). This perhaps shows a combobox on project open, but also allows users to move group.
2. The tasks assigned to a group are highlighted for the user, depending on which group they selected. Clicking on a task area within a group no longer does assignment - it just uncovers the features inside that task.
3. Button to mark a task as "fully mapped" - this signals to other mappers via symbology that it doesn't need more work, but doesn't block people from still mapping, e.g. adding a new building. We can use the existing *tada* animation.

### Additional thoughts / v2 ideas

4. Button to "reassign" a task to another group (tasks can be pre-assigned via FieldTM + QFC, but it's possible to modify afterwards inside QField)
5. The "reassign" comments are stored as events. The most recent reassign is used as current symbology.

title: feat(splitter): add split-by-roads task splitting algorithm
body:
Closes hotosm/field-tm#3107

## Summary
- Adds a new `SPLIT_BY_ROADS` splitting algorithm for projects collecting street-level data (e.g. imagery), where mappers walk/cycle roads rather than visiting individual buildings.
- Reuses the existing linear-features polygonize step (`common/1-linear-features.sql`, which already unions roads/rivers/railways/aeroways/non-traversable barriers with the AOI boundary and runs `ST_Polygonize`) directly as the final output, skipping the building-clustering/alignment steps (2-5) entirely.
- New `algorithms/split_by_roads.sql` extract query, mirroring `common/6-extract.sql` but sourcing `polygonsnocount` directly, with `building_count` computed against `ways_poly` for informational purposes.
- Refactors `SplittingAlgorithm` to expose a `sql_files` property (ordered SQL pipeline per algorithm) instead of hardcoding the 6-file list inline in `splitter.py`.
- Fixes a latent bug in `_resolve_algorithm_params`: it previously raised "requires the following parameters" even when an algorithm's `required_params` was empty, if no legacy `num_buildings`/`num_enumerators` args were passed. Didn't affect existing algorithms (all have non-empty required params) but is needed for `SPLIT_BY_ROADS` (zero required params) to work correctly.
- Wires the new algorithm into `project_services.py::split_aoi`, the step4 splitting UI dropdown, and the JS param-visibility logic.
- Adds docs following the existing per-algorithm convention: `docs/algorithms/roads.md`, a short new section in `docs/pipeline.md`, a bullet in the package `README.md`, and a new section + table row in the user-facing `docs/manuals/task-splitting.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `docker compose -f compose.test.yaml run --rm backend pytest package_tests/test_area_splitter` — 46/46 passed, including two new tests for `SPLIT_BY_ROADS` (one exercising the `_resolve_algorithm_params` fix via a monkeypatched call, one running the real SQL pipeline against the `kathmandu_extract.geojson` fixture and asserting valid Polygon/MultiPolygon output).

title: feat(auth): use the shared Hanko login component in the header
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [x] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [x] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Related Issue

Fixes #3038

## Describe this PR

Wires Field-TM into the shared HOT login (Hanko SSO), the same way the other
HOT apps do it.

Until now the header had its own `<wa-button id="login-btn">` that redirected to
the login page by hand, and the `<hotosm-auth>` web component was hidden away in
a `display: none` div purely to validate the session after the redirect back.
This PR drops the custom button and puts `<hotosm-auth>` in the header slot
directly, so the shared component renders both states: the login button when
logged out, and the user profile dropdown with logout when logged in.

Two things run off the component's `hanko-login` event, both guarded so
navigation doesn't re-trigger them:

1. **User sync** — registers/syncs the authenticated user into the Field-TM
   database via `/api/v1/auth/profile/me`, once per browser session
   (`sessionStorage`). Same behaviour as before, just moved.
2. **Language adoption (#3038)** — reads the user's language from their HOT
   login profile and applies it via `?lang=`, which the existing locale
   middleware persists into the `ftm_locale` cookie. This is one-way
   (login → Field-TM) and only fires when the profile language *changes*: we
   remember the last value we saw in `localStorage`, so a profile change shows
   up on the next load, while a manual choice in the language switcher is
   respected as long as the profile language stays put.

On logout both flags are cleared, so a different user logging in on the same
browser gets a fresh sync and their own language.

Also included: a `deploy-testlogin.yml` workflow and `compose.testlogin.yaml`
that stand up the test environment described below, pointing at
`dev.login.hotosm.org`.

## AI Tool Usage

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (complete below)

**If AI-assisted:**

- Tool(s) used: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5)

## Screenshots

N/A — the header login button and profile dropdown are the shared component's
own UI, unchanged apart from the brand colour noted below.

## Alternative Approaches Considered

**Theming the login button.** The obvious way to colour it was
`--login-btn-bg-color: var(--ftm-brand)`, but `--ftm-brand` is itself
`var(--hot-color-primary-600)`, and that nested indirection resolves
inconsistently once inherited into the component's shadow DOM — it fell back to
gray-600. So the CSS sets the HOT red as a literal `#d73f3f`. Only the login
button is affected; the profile dropdown keeps the component's defaults.

**Syncing language both ways.** Deliberately not done. Pushing a Field-TM
switcher choice back up to the login profile would make the central profile
mutable from every app, and two apps disagreeing would fight over it. One-way
adoption with change-detection gives the useful behaviour (your profile language
follows you into Field-TM) without that.

## Review Guide

**A live test environment is deployed from this branch:**
👉 **https://fieldtm.testlogin.hotosm.org**

It runs against `dev.login.hotosm.org` for auth, so you can log in with a dev
Hanko account and exercise the whole flow without touching production. It
redeploys automatically on every push to this branch.

Worth checking there:

- Logged out → the header shows the red **Login** button; clicking it takes you
  to the central login page and returns you to where you were.
- Logged in → the button is replaced by the profile dropdown, and logout works
  from it.
- First login → the user appears in the Field-TM database (the profile sync).
- Set a language on your HOT login profile, then reload Field-TM → the UI
  switches to it.
- Then change the language with Field-TM's own switcher and navigate around →
  your manual choice sticks, it doesn't get overwritten on every page load.
- Log out and back in as a different user with a different profile language →
  you get theirs, not the previous user's.

title: feat(chart): add bundled Hanko auth to the Kubernetes deployment
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [x] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [ ] ✅ Test
- [ ] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Related Issue

Related to #3032

## Describe this PR

Adds an `auth.bundled` section to the Helm chart that deploys a self-hosted
Hanko instance alongside field-tm - a Deployment/Service for Hanko itself,
plus its own dedicated in-cluster PostGIS database (Deployment/Service/PVC),
mirroring the existing `deploy/compose.login.yaml` overlay used for the
non-k8s deployment path. When `auth.bundled.enabled=true`, the backend
Deployment's `HANKO_API_URL` env var is automatically pointed at the new
in-cluster Hanko service.

The Hanko config file mixes plain settings with secret material (the signing
key, db password, SMTP/OAuth credentials), so instead of the envsubst +
init-container approach the compose overlay uses to render it, it's rendered
as a `Secret` directly via Helm templating (`chart/templates/hanko-secret.yaml`)
against `auth.bundled.config`/`auth.bundled.secret` values - Helm already does
that substitution declaratively, so the extra render step isn't needed in k8s.

`auth.bundled.secret.hankoSecret` is required (via a `required` guard,
matching the existing `ingress.host` pattern) whenever `auth.bundled.enabled`
is `true`, rather than shipping a well-known default signing key.

### Scope

This is the base slice: Hanko's own Deployment/Service/config/database. It
does **not** include:

- Ingress routing for a public `login.<domain>` host. The chart currently
  only models a single ingress host for field-tm itself
  (`chart/templates/ingress.yaml`); giving Hanko its own host needs either a
  second `Ingress` resource or a shared one with path/host rules, which felt
  like its own design decision worth separating from the base packaging.
- SMTP / Google OAuth wiring beyond what's already exposed under
  `auth.bundled.config`/`auth.bundled.secret`.

Filing it this way so the base pieces (which are the bulk of the surface
area, and independently useful once you're proxying to the Hanko service
yourself) can land first.

## AI Tool Usage

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (complete below)

**If AI-assisted:**

- Tool(s) used: Claude Code
- What was generated: initial draft of the chart templates, values.yaml
  keys, and README docs, based on reading the existing chart patterns
  (`db.enabled` toggle, `qfieldQgis` optional-service pattern) and
  `deploy/compose.login.yaml`.
- What you reviewed and changed: read every generated template against the
  existing chart conventions, fixed a real bug where the Hanko `migrate`/
  `serve` containers used `command:` (which replaces the image's
  `ENTRYPOINT /hanko` and made both crash-loop with "executable file not
  found") instead of `args:`, and verified the whole thing end-to-end on a
  local kind cluster before opening this PR (see Review Guide).

## Screenshots

N/A - this is backend/infra config, no UI change.

## Alternative Approaches Considered

**Reusing `contrib/login/hanko-config.tpl.yaml` as-is.** That file is an
envsubst template tied to the docker-compose init-container pattern. Helm
already renders values declaratively, so wiring the same file through `tpl`
would mean fighting two templating syntaxes (`${VAR}` vs `{{ }}`) for no
benefit - a native Helm `Secret` template covering the same fields is
simpler and keeps the k8s and compose paths independently readable.

**A single shared Postgres for both field-tm and Hanko.** Compose runs a
dedicated `hanko-db` alongside the main db, so this chart does the same
(`auth.bundled.db`, separate from the existing `db` key) rather than
introducing shared-database coupling between two otherwise-independent
services.

## Review Guide

With a local Hanko secret set, `helm template`/`helm lint` should pass
cleanly, and installing with `auth.bundled.enabled=true` should render:
`hanko-secret` (Secret), `hanko-db` (Deployment/Service/PVC), and `hanko`
(Deployment/Service). Omitting `auth.bundled.secret.hankoSecret` while
`auth.bundled.enabled=true` should fail the render with a clear error instead
of silently deploying with no signing key.

I verified this locally on a throwaway `kind` cluster: installed the chart
with `auth.bundled.enabled=true` and a generated `hankoSecret`, and confirmed
`hanko-db` reached Ready, the `hanko-migrate` init container completed
successfully, the `hanko` container logged `http server started on [::]:8000`
`http server started on [::]:8001`, a curl pod inside the cluster got a `200`
from `http://<release>-hanko:8000/.well-known/jwks.json`, and the new
`hanko-test-connection` helm test hook completed successfully.
