title: just start dev fails: ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug does not exist
body:
## Description

The documented local dev quick start fails on a completely fresh clone:

```sh
just config generate-dotenv
just start dev
```

`just start dev` runs `AUTH_PROVIDER=disabled docker compose up -d` against the root `compose.yaml`, whose `api` and `migrations` services default to:

```
image: "ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:${TAG_OVERRIDE:-debug}"
```

`just config generate-dotenv` does not set `TAG_OVERRIDE`, so this resolves to `ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug` - which does not exist in the registry.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hotosm/field-tm.git
cd field-tm
just config generate-dotenv
just start dev
```

## Actual result

```
Image ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug Pulling
Image ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug failed to resolve reference "ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug": ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug: not found
error: recipe `dev` failed with exit code 1
```

Confirmed independently against the registry (not a local caching issue):

```sh
$ docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/hotosm/field-tm:debug
manifest unknown

$ gh api "/orgs/hotosm/packages/container/field-tm/versions?per_page=100" --jq '.[].metadata.container.tags[]' | sort -u
2026.3
2026.3.6
2026.4
2026.4.0
2026.4.1
2026.4.2
2026.4.3
ci-dev
ci-main
latest
login_hanko_v2
```

No version of the `hotosm/field-tm` package has ever been tagged `debug`.

## Likely cause

`debug` is a Dockerfile build **stage** name (`src/Dockerfile:178`, `FROM runtime-base AS debug`), not a published tag. `.github/workflows/build_ci_img.yml` builds and pushes the `ci` stage (`FROM debug AS ci`, `src/Dockerfile:216`) under `ci-${branch}` (e.g. `ci-dev`, which does exist), but nothing publishes the `debug` stage itself under a `debug` tag. `compose.yaml`'s default looks like it's referencing a tag that was never (or is no longer) published, rather than `ci-dev`.

## Expected result

`just start dev` on a fresh clone should pull a real image and come up, per the README's documented "Local development" quick start.

## Workaround

`TAG_OVERRIDE=ci-dev` in `.env` before `just start dev` gets past this specific error (the underlying `ci` image extends the `debug` stage, so it's a compatible substitute).

## Environment

- `docker --version`: Docker Desktop, macOS (arm64) - though the missing tag itself is registry-side and platform-independent; I confirmed via `docker manifest inspect` and the GHCR package API directly, not just a local pull failure.
- Field-TM commit: `68feb4d05306dd4b58110721d027fba0d1f0acf0` (dev)

title: KeyError 500 in convert-odk-submission-json-to-geojson on submissions missing meta/__id/__system
body:
## Description

`POST /api/v1/helpers/convert-odk-submission-json-to-geojson` throws an unhandled `KeyError` (500) for any submission object missing one of `meta`, `__id`, or `__system` - which the endpoint's own docstring says can happen, since it explicitly accepts submission JSON "downloaded via ODK Central, **or osm-fieldwork**".

```python
# src/backend/app/central/central_crud.py:582-586, in convert_odk_submission_json_to_geojson
for submission in submission_json:
    # Remove unnecessary keys
    keys_to_remove = ["meta", "__id", "__system"]
    for key in keys_to_remove:
        submission.pop(key)
```

`dict.pop(key)` with no default raises `KeyError` if the key isn't present. There's no `try/except` around this, and the route handler (`src/backend/app/helpers/helper_routes.py:181-210`) doesn't catch it either, so it propagates as an unhandled 500.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in (the route only requires `login_required`, no project-manager role).
2. `POST /api/v1/helpers/convert-odk-submission-json-to-geojson` with a multipart `data` file containing:
   ```json
   [{"foo": "bar"}]
   ```

## Actual result

500 Internal Server Error, unhandled `KeyError: 'meta'`.

## Expected result

Either the endpoint should validate/require the expected shape up front and return a 422 with a clear message (consistent with the 422s already used elsewhere in this function, e.g. the "Project contains no submissions yet" case just above it), or use `submission.pop(key, None)` so a genuinely optional/absent key doesn't crash the whole request.

## Environment

Field-TM commit: `68feb4d05306dd4b58110721d027fba0d1f0acf0` (dev). Verified by reading the exact code path (`helper_routes.py` -> `central_crud.convert_odk_submission_json_to_geojson`); the full docker stack wasn't runnable on this machine (see #3128), so this is traced statically rather than hit over HTTP, but the logic is deterministic - any dict lacking one of those three keys unconditionally raises.

title: save_data_extract never actually resets task_areas_geojson (exclude_none drops the None write)
body:
## Description

Re-uploading a data extract is meant to reset the project's existing task split, but it silently doesn't - the old `task_areas_geojson` stays in the database, now desynced from the new extract.

```python
# src/backend/app/projects/project_services.py:892-901, save_data_extract
await DbProject.update(
    db,
    project_id,
    project_schemas.ProjectUpdate(
        data_extract_geojson=geojson_data,
        # Reset split status when a new extract is accepted.
        task_areas_geojson=None,
    ),
)
```

`DbProject.update` builds its `SET` clause from `dump_and_check_model(project_update)` (`src/backend/app/db/models.py:663-668`), which calls:

```python
model_dump = db_model.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude_unset=True)
```

`exclude_none=True` strips **any** field whose value is `None` from the dump, regardless of whether it was explicitly passed (as here) or just left at its default - Pydantic's `exclude_unset` tracks "was this field assigned during construction", not "is this a meaningful null write". So `task_areas_geojson` never appears in `model_dump`, the generated `UPDATE ... SET` never mentions that column, and the existing value in the DB is left untouched.

## Reproduction (verified by direct execution, no DB needed - this is a pure Pydantic behavior)

```python
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ProjectUpdate(BaseModel):
    data_extract_geojson: Optional[dict] = None
    task_areas_geojson: Optional[dict] = None

update = ProjectUpdate(
    data_extract_geojson={"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [1]},
    task_areas_geojson=None,
)
dump = update.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude_unset=True)
print(dump)                                  # {'data_extract_geojson': {...}}
print("task_areas_geojson" in dump)          # False
```

The `task_areas_geojson=None` the caller passed never survives to reach SQL.

## Actual result

After uploading a new data extract over a project that was already split into tasks, `task_areas_geojson` still holds the old task boundaries. The UI/API continues to serve the stale split, now geometrically and semantically out of sync with the new extract (buildings assigned to tasks that no longer make sense for the new data, `has_task_areas` still true when it should require re-splitting, etc).

## Expected result

The comment's intent: replacing the data extract should clear the old task split so the project goes back to needing a fresh split.

## Suggested fix

Use an explicit sentinel/flag rather than relying on `exclude_none` to carry a real null-write (e.g. a `fields_to_null: set[str]` param on `DbProject.update`, or drop `exclude_none` and handle "don't touch this field" via `exclude_unset` alone with every truly-optional field always passed explicitly). Whatever the fix, this same footgun likely affects any other caller that expects `SomeField=None` to null out a column via this pattern - worth grepping for.

## Environment

Field-TM commit: `68feb4d05306dd4b58110721d027fba0d1f0acf0` (dev). Verified the Pydantic behavior by direct execution (above); traced the SQL-building path (`dump_and_check_model` -> `_project_update_placeholders` -> `UPDATE ... SET {placeholders}`) by reading `db/models.py` - the full docker stack wasn't runnable here (see #3128) to additionally confirm against a live database, but the mechanism is deterministic given the reproduced Pydantic output.

title: ftm_locale cookie middleware uses raw string match, disagreeing with resolve_locale's normalization
body:
## Description

`?lang=` sets the page's locale for the current request via one matching function, but persists it via `ftm_locale` cookie using a different, stricter check - so any `lang` value that only matches through normalization or base-language fallback renders correctly once, but is never remembered.

The two code paths disagree:

```python
# src/backend/app/i18n.py:170-189, resolve_locale (decides what the page renders)
lang = request.query_params.get("lang")
matched_query_locale = match_supported_locale(lang) if lang else None
if matched_query_locale:
    return matched_query_locale
...

# src/backend/app/i18n.py:100-109, match_supported_locale
def match_supported_locale(locale: str) -> str | None:
    normalized_locale = normalize_locale_code(locale)   # .lower().replace("-", "_")
    if normalized_locale in SUPPORTED_LOCALES:
        return normalized_locale
    base_language = normalized_locale.split("_", 1)[0]   # base-language fallback
    if base_language in SUPPORTED_LOCALES:
        return base_language
    return None
```

```python
# src/backend/app/i18n.py:230-241, create_locale_cookie_middleware (decides what gets persisted)
lang = lang_values[0] if lang_values else None
if not lang or lang not in SUPPORTED_LOCALES:   # raw string, no normalization, no fallback
    await app(scope, receive, send)
    return
```

## Reproduction (verified by direct execution of the same logic)

```python
def normalize_locale_code(locale):
    return locale.strip().lower().replace("-", "_")

SUPPORTED_LOCALES = ["en", "es", "fr", "pt", "pt_br", "ar"]  # subset, matches src/backend/app/locales/*

def match_supported_locale(locale):
    normalized = normalize_locale_code(locale)
    if normalized in SUPPORTED_LOCALES:
        return normalized
    base = normalized.split("_", 1)[0]
    if base in SUPPORTED_LOCALES:
        return base
    return None

for lang in ["PT-BR", "fr-CA", "en-US"]:
    print(lang, "-> resolve_locale picks:", match_supported_locale(lang),
          "| cookie middleware sets cookie:", lang in SUPPORTED_LOCALES)
```

Output:

```
PT-BR -> resolve_locale picks: pt_br | cookie middleware sets cookie: False
fr-CA -> resolve_locale picks: fr    | cookie middleware sets cookie: False
en-US -> resolve_locale picks: en    | cookie middleware sets cookie: False
```

## Steps to reproduce against the app

1. Visit any page with `?lang=PT-BR` (a real, hyphenated, mixed-case tag - the form a browser or an external system is more likely to send than the internal `pt_br` key).
2. The page renders in Portuguese (Brazil), since `resolve_locale` normalizes it correctly.
3. No `ftm_locale` cookie is set (raw `"PT-BR"` isn't in `SUPPORTED_LOCALES`).
4. Navigate to any page without `?lang=` - the language silently reverts to the `Accept-Language`/default resolution instead of staying on the choice just made.

## Why this matters now

PR #3118 (adopting the user's language from their HOT login profile) drives this exact `?lang=` param from `profile.language.toLowerCase()` - a value from an external system, so it's not guaranteed to already be in the internal `pt_br`-style format. If it ever comes through hyphenated or as a country-qualified variant, this bug means the adopted language never actually sticks past the one page load.

## Expected result

The cookie middleware should persist whatever `resolve_locale`/`match_supported_locale` actually resolved to (e.g. reuse `match_supported_locale(lang)` and store its return value), not the raw query value compared against the internal key format.

## Environment

Field-TM commit: `68feb4d05306dd4b58110721d027fba0d1f0acf0` (dev). Verified by directly executing the normalization/matching logic as shown above (no server needed - both functions are pure). Related: #3038 (adopting locale from HOT login), PR #3118 (implements that, and is the first caller likely to hit this).

title: Updates to QField public project roles
body:
1. It's now possible to set the default role of external / non-collaborator users. Previously it was `reader` only, meaning people had to be invited as collaborators before they could edit. It's technically possible to make public projects editable by anyone that is logged in now (default role = editor).
2. It's now also possible to add non org member collaborators to projects. This used to work only for personal accounts, so I was temporarily using `spwoodcock` as the 'organisation'. Now we can switch batch to `HOTOSM` as the org project owner, and invite project collaborators, without needing to add every used to the org first.

title: Mapping app: consider integration possibilities with DHIS2
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Alerted to the presence of this app recently: apparently the most used health management info system throughout Africa.
- Have also had prompts suggesting we could possibly integrate with the ecosystem they have built somehow, and leverage their excellent work.
- https://github.com/dhis2 looks like a Java backend server and a Kotlin / Android mobile app is used, but I haven't explored further, installed, or tested.
- Lots of Ministries of Health throughout the continent probably have varying degrees of health service + population data stored here, so if we can (1) improve the ease of data collection (e.g. via task splitting), and data model for into into the system (2) add possible integrations for export of the data and packaging for supplementing e.g. HDX and OSM.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

1. Install, investigate, and analyse what the offering is, and why it's so popular - is it a good ecosystem to get involved with?
2. Assess possible integration surfaces with their tooling, if we can e.g. add a task coord layer on top of their mobile app (and do they already handle this in any way?).
3. Look at the structure of the data stored in their ecosystem (the server db, basically) and what formats they export to. Is there scope of add simple exporters for extraction and combining with existing datasets such as OSM, or perhaps packaging for useful datasets on platforms like HDX?

**Additional context**

- Surprised we haven't covered this already here: https://docs.field.hotosm.org/about/faq/#dont-other-tools-do-similar-things
- Perhaps because it's so health data specific, and not a generic field data collection tool, we didn't consider it before?

title: feat(htmx): add "Projects near me" sort to the project list
body:
## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)

- [x] 🍕 Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug Fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🧑‍💻 Refactor
- [x] ✅ Test
- [ ] 🤖 Build or CI
- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Related Issue

Fixes #2113

## Describe this PR

Mappers need to be near a project to contribute, but the project list gives no way to find nearby work. This adds a **"Projects near me"** button to the project list. On click, the browser asks for the user's location (normal permission prompt); the list is then sorted by distance to each project's outline, and each card shows "N km away" / "Less than 1 km away".

This follows the approach suggested in #2113: user-initiated only, no notifications, and no user location stored.

- Coordinates are rounded to 2 decimals (~1 km) in the browser and again on the server, used for a single query, never persisted.
- No schema change: distance is computed on the fly with `ST_Distance(outline::geography, point::geography)` (0 when the point is inside the outline).
- `DbProject.all()` gets an optional `near=(lat, lon)` used together with `sort_by="nearest"`; all other sorts are unchanged and ignore the point.
- Invalid/missing coordinates (non-numeric, NaN/inf, out of range) silently fall back to the default sort.
- Pagination links and the status/search filters keep the location sort (hidden `lat`/`lon` inputs).
- The only JS is the geolocation call (needs the browser API); the server stays authoritative and renders the sorted page.

## AI Tool Usage

- [ ] **0** - No AI at any point
- [ ] **1** - AI helped me think, but I wrote all the code myself
- [ ] **2** - I planned the change and decided the approach; AI helped write the code
- [ ] **3** - AI planned and wrote it; I checked and approved each step as it went
- [x] **4** - I set the AI going and left it to it; I reviewed the finished result
- [ ] **5** - I set the AI going and left it to it; nobody has read the result - no review, or AI review only

- Tool(s) used: Claude Code
- What was generated: all code, tests and this description
- What you reviewed and changed: I reviewed the diff and the test results, and went through an explanation of each change before submitting.

## Screenshots

<!-- drag & drop: after.png (desktop, sorted by distance), denied-mobile.png (mobile, location denied) -->

## Alternative Approaches Considered

- **Notify users when a project is created near them** (original issue idea): rejected per maintainer feedback. It is intrusive and needs stored user locations.
- **Store an optional home location on the user profile:** avoided for privacy and to keep this PR schema-free.
- **KNN `<->` ordering on the GiST index:** faster on large tables, but geometry distance is in degrees and would mis-order results at higher latitudes. `ST_Distance` on geography is exact and fine for the project-table size; it can be optimised later if needed.
- **Free-text place search ("near Nairobi"):** useful follow-up, but needs a geocoding service, so left out of this PR.

## Review Guide

1. `just start dev`, create or ensure a few projects with outlines in different places.
2. Open `/projects`, click **Projects near me**, allow location → list sorted by distance with "km away" on cards; "Nearest to me" selected in Sort By.
3. Change the status filter or page → stays sorted by distance.
4. Deny location (or block it in browser settings) → warning callout, list unchanged.
5. Manually try `/projects?sort=nearest&lat=abc&lon=1` → falls back to newest.

Tests: `src/backend/tests/htmx/test_project_list_nearest.py` (14 tests: DB-backed ordering and distances, rendering, rounding, pagination, invalid input fallback). Full backend suite passes locally except the ODK Central / QGIS-dependent tests (`test_central_crud.py`, `test_qfield_project_gen_svc.py`), which fail identically on `dev` without these services.

New translatable strings are not yet in `field_tm.pot`; a fresh `just i18n extract` would have pulled in many unrelated pending strings, so I left that to the usual i18n chore commit. Happy to add it here if preferred.

title: PR Test Backend and pre-commit.ci fail on every PR since ~Oct 19 — root causes and fixes
body:
The backend test workflow has failed on every run since #1645 (55 failures, ~48 min). From the logs of the hotosm/field-tm#3141 run I traced four causes and prepared fixes on a branch: https://github.com/luxlepus/field-tm/compare/dev...luxlepus:field-tm:fix/ci-test-failures

1) 35 × 401 Unauthorized — since 5c00a25, DEBUG no longer implies the local admin (good). But the test stack builds .env from .env.example (AUTH_PROVIDER=bundled), and most tests implicitly expected the local admin. Fix: an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py pins AUTH_PROVIDER=disabled; login_as still opts into auth. No change to the auth model itself.

2) 9 × ImportError in test_qfield_project_gen_svc.py — register_plugin_data_dirs moved to the worker’s utils.py, but the test stub for utils didn’t include it. Fix: load the real (stdlib-only) utils.py for it.

3) 11 area-splitter failures + the ~48 min runtime — two real bugs in splitBySQL:
split_by_roads.sql runs a DO block before its final SELECT; psycopg starts at the first result, so fetching fails with command status: DO. Fix: advance to the last result set.
On any error the transaction was left open, so the transaction advisory lock stayed held and every later split waited for the 270 s statement timeout. Fix: roll back (and close our own connection) on failure, plus a regression test that fails without it.
Also: the CLI passed --number/--tasks as strings, which _sql_literal rejects (type=int).

4) pre-commit.ci — ruff E501 on two docstrings in area_splitter/__init__.py.
Locally, with the CI settings (DEBUG=True, AUTH_PROVIDER=bundled): tests/ 390 passed (only the ODK Central tests could not run without Central), area-splitter 48 passed (the remaining 3 need the raw-data API / CI DB host), osm-fieldwork 63 passed; all pre-commit hooks pass with --all-files.

Happy to open this as a PR (four separate commits), or feel free to cherry-pick.

title: Inject team names from HOT login into the task splitter
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

- Currently we can open the task splitter with an AOI loaded
- HOT login has the concept of organisations and teams
- When creating a FieldTM project, we should have the option to import teams from HOT login into the project
- We want to re-use these existing team names in the task splitting assignment

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- During project creation, search and add teams to the project.
- When going to the task splitting and assignment ui, instead of only allowing entering new team names freeform, we should also add a list of available teams to assign to a task.
- The teams are likely injected via the URL params somehow, perhaps via an API call, as we don't want to have to rely on APIs for the default standalone task splitting ui (it's frontend only in most scenarios)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Just a rough idea, perhaps more thought needed.

title: Task Planner: let users download the AOI as GeoJSON
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In the Task Planner I draw an area on the Area tab. On the next tab, Data, I need to upload features for that area. I can get them from an export tool, but the export tool needs the area as a file, and I can't get my drawn area out of the planner. Downloads only exist for tasks, after splitting, and the only other way out is the whole task plan on the Export step. So I either have to draw the same area again somewhere else, or split first just to get the shape back.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Let me download the area I drew. Clicking the area on the map in the Area tab could open a small popup, like the one tasks get after splitting, with a download button. GeoJSON is the main thing I need. A GPX outline would be a nice extra, but it isn't needed.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A "Download area" button in the Area tab sidebar would also work. I leaned towards the popup because tasks already work that way.

**Additional context**
I already have this working locally and plan to open a PR for it.
